title.en: Volume 459 Biographies 218: Recluses 3: Xu Zhongxing, Su Yunqing, Qiao Ding, Wang Zhongmin, Liu Mianzhi, Hu Xian, Guo Yong, Liu Yu, Wei Shanzhi, an Shitong, Zhuo Xing, Liu Tingshi, Chao Gu, Xu Ji, Ceng Shuqing, Liu Yongyi

sentences.zh: 隱逸下

translations.literal: Recluses, Part Two
translations.idiomatic: Recluses (continued)

sentences.zh: ○徐中行蘇雲卿譙定王忠民劉勉之胡憲郭雍劉愚魏掞之安世通

translations.literal: ○ Xu Zhongxing, Su Yunqing, Qiao Ding, Wang Zhongmin, Liu Mianzhi, Hu Xian, Guo Yong, Liu Yu, Wei Shanzhi, An Shitong
translations.idiomatic: ○ Xu Zhongxing, Su Yunqing, Qiao Ding, Wang Zhongmin, Liu Mianzhi, Hu Xian, Guo Yong, Liu Yu, Wei Shanzhi, and An Shitong

sentences.zh: 徐中行，台州臨海人。

translations.literal: Xu Zhongxing was a man of Linhai in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhongxing was from Linhai in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 始知學，聞安定胡瑗講明道學，其徒轉相傳授，將往從焉。

translations.literal: When he first came to know learning, he heard that Hu Yuan of Dingzhou lectured on the learning of the Clear Way, and that his disciples passed it on to one another in turn; he was about to go and follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took up study, he heard that Hu Yuan of Dingzhou taught the Cheng Hao school of learning, whose disciples handed it down from one to another, and he set out to join them.

sentences.zh: 至京師，首謁範純仁，純仁賢之，薦於司馬光，光謂斯人神清氣和，可與進道。

translations.literal: On reaching the capital he first called on Fan Chunren, who regarded him as worthy and recommended him to Sima Guang; Guang said this man's spirit was clear and his bearing harmonious, and that he could advance together on the Way.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he first visited Fan Chunren, who esteemed him and recommended him to Sima Guang, who said the man had a clear spirit and gentle air and could walk the path of learning with them.

sentences.zh: 會福唐劉彝赴闕，得瑗所授經，熟讀精思，攻苦食淡，夏不扇，冬不爐，夜不安枕者逾年。

translations.literal: It happened that Liu Yi of Futang went to court, obtained the classics Hu Yuan had transmitted, read them closely and thought deeply, toiled in hardship and ate plain food, used no fan in summer and no brazier in winter, and for more than a year did not lay his head on a pillow at night.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi of Futang happened to go to court, received the classics Hu Yuan had taught, and read them with close attention; he lived in austerity—no fan in summer, no brazier in winter—and for more than a year slept without a pillow.

sentences.zh: 乃歸葺小室，竟日危坐，所造詣人莫測也。

translations.literal: He then returned, repaired a small room, and sat upright all day; the depth he reached no one could fathom.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home, built a small study, and sat upright all day long; how far his attainment went, no one could tell.

sentences.zh: 父死，跣足廬墓，躬耕養母。

translations.literal: When his father died, he went barefoot and kept a mourning hut at the tomb, personally plowing the fields to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he went barefoot, kept vigil at the tomb, and farmed by hand to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 推其餘力，葬內外親及州裏貧無後者十餘喪。

translations.literal: With his remaining strength he buried more than ten coffins of relatives within and without the family, and of the poor in the prefecture who had no heirs.
translations.idiomatic: With whatever strength remained he arranged burial for more than ten kin and neighbors in the prefecture who were poor and left no descendants.

sentences.zh: 晚年教授學者，自灑掃應對、格物致知達於治國平天下，不失其性，不越其序而後已。

translations.literal: In his later years he instructed scholars, from sweeping and responding through investigating things and extending knowledge up to ordering the state and bringing peace to the realm, not departing from their nature and not overstepping their proper sequence, and only then stopping.
translations.idiomatic: In later life he taught students the full curriculum—from sweeping and polite response through investigating things and extending knowledge to ordering the state and pacifying the world—without letting them lose their nature or skip stages.

sentences.zh: 其友羅適持節本路，舉以自代，又率部使者以遺逸薦。

translations.literal: His friend Luo Shi, holding credentials in this circuit, recommended him to succeed himself, and also led the circuit commissioners to recommend him as a hidden worthy.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Luo Shi, then commissioner of the circuit, nominated him as his successor and also led the circuit envoys to recommend him as a recluse of outstanding merit.

sentences.zh: 崇寧中，郡守李諤又以八行薦。

translations.literal: In the Chongning era the prefect Li E again recommended him on the Eight Virtuous Conducts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongning period the prefect Li E again nominated him under the Eight Virtuous Conducts program.

sentences.zh: 時章、蔡竊國柄，竄逐善類且盡，中行每一聞命輒淚下。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang and Cai usurped control of the state; worthy men were driven out until almost none remained, and whenever Zhongxing heard of an appointment he would shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun and Cai Jing then held the reins of power and had driven out nearly all the good men; each time Zhongxing heard of a summons he wept.

sentences.zh: 一日，去之黃岩，會親友，盡毀其所為文，幅巾藜杖，往來委羽山中。

translations.literal: One day he left for Huangyan, met kin and friends, destroyed all the writings he had made, wore a plain headcloth and carried a staff of ramie, and went back and forth in the Weiyu Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: One day he went to Huangyan, gathered kin and friends, burned all his writings, took up plain dress and a ramie staff, and wandered in the Weiyu Mountains.

sentences.zh: 客有詰以避舉要名者，中行曰：“人而無行，與禽獸等。

translations.literal: A guest questioned him, saying he avoided recommendation to court fame; Zhongxing said, "A man without conduct is the equal of birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: When a visitor accused him of shunning office to win a reputation, Zhongxing said, "A man without moral conduct is no better than an animal.

sentences.zh: 使吾得以八行應科目，則彼之不被舉者非人類與？

translations.literal: If I were able to answer the Eight Conducts examination, would those who were not recommended not be human beings?
translations.idiomatic: If I could qualify under the Eight Conducts, would everyone who failed to qualify cease to be human?

sentences.zh: 吾正欲避此名，非要名也。”

translations.literal: I precisely wish to avoid this reputation; I do not seek reputation.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to avoid that kind of fame—I am not chasing fame."

sentences.zh: 客慚而退。

translations.literal: The guest withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: The visitor withdrew, ashamed.

sentences.zh: 陳瓘謫台州，聞名納交，暨其沒，錄其行事，謂與山陽徐積齊名，呼為“八行先生”。

translations.literal: Chen Guan was banished to Taizhou, heard his name and sought his friendship; when Guan died, he recorded his conduct, saying he was of equal fame with Xu Ji of Shanyang, and called him "Master of the Eight Conducts."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guan, exiled to Taizhou, sought him out by reputation; after Guan's death he recorded Zhongxing's life and said he ranked with Xu Ji of Shanyang, calling him "Master of the Eight Conducts."

sentences.zh: 子三人，庭筠其季也，童草有誌行，事父兄孝友天至。

translations.literal: He had three sons; Tingyun was the youngest, and even as a child showed purpose and will, serving father and elder brothers with natural filial piety and brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons; the youngest, Tingyun, showed purpose even as a boy and served his father and brothers with instinctive filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 居喪毀甚，既免喪，不忍娶者十餘年。

translations.literal: In mourning he was greatly emaciated; after the mourning period ended he could not bring himself to marry for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He grieved his father's death so deeply that for more than ten years after mourning ended he could not bring himself to marry.

sentences.zh: 秦檜當國，科場尚諛佞，試題問中興歌頌，庭筠歎曰：“今日豈歌頌時耶！”

translations.literal: When Qin Hui held power the examination halls favored flattery; the examination topic asked for songs praising the restoration, and Tingyun sighed, "Is today really a time for songs of praise!"
translations.idiomatic: With Qin Hui in power the examinations favored flattery; when the topic asked for odes celebrating restoration, Tingyun sighed, "Is this an age for celebration?"

sentences.zh: 疏其未足為中興者五，見者尤之，庭筠曰：“吾欲不妄語，而敢欺君乎？”

translations.literal: He set forth five points in which restoration was still insufficient; those who saw it blamed him, and Tingyun said, "I wish not to speak falsely—how dare I deceive the ruler?
translations.idiomatic: He listed five reasons restoration was still incomplete; critics blamed him, but Tingyun said, "I will not speak falsely—how could I deceive the throne?

sentences.zh: 黃岩尉鄭伯熊代去，請益，庭筠曰：“富貴易得，名節難守。

translations.literal: Zheng Boxiong of Huangyan, when his term as district defender ended, asked for instruction; Tingyun said, "Wealth and honor are easily obtained; name and integrity are hard to keep.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Boxiong of Huangyan was leaving office, he asked for counsel; Tingyun said, "Wealth and rank come easily; reputation and integrity are hard to keep.

sentences.zh: 願安時處順，主張世道。”

translations.literal: I hope you will rest in the times and abide in what is fitting, and uphold the moral order of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Stay steady in troubled times and uphold the moral order of the world."

sentences.zh: 伯熊受其言，迄為名臣。

translations.literal: Boxiong accepted his words and in the end became a famous minister.
translations.idiomatic: Boxiong took his advice and in the end became a noted statesman.

sentences.zh: 有詔舉人嚐五上春官者予嶽祠。

translations.literal: An edict provided that candidates who had five times presented themselves at the spring examinations were to be given posts at mountain shrines.
translations.idiomatic: An edict offered mountain-shrine appointments to candidates who had failed the metropolitan examination five times.

sentences.zh: 庭筠適應格，所親鹹勸之，庭筠辭曰：“ 吾嚐草封事，謂嶽廟冗祿無用。

translations.literal: Tingyun happened to qualify; those close to him all urged him, but Tingyun declined, saying, "I once drafted a memorial saying that redundant stipends at mountain shrines were useless.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyun happened to qualify; friends urged him to accept, but he refused: "I once drafted a memorial calling shrine stipends useless surplus.

sentences.zh: 既心非之，可躬蹈耶？”

translations.literal: Since in my heart I opposed it, how could I practice it in person?
translations.idiomatic: If I opposed it in principle, how could I take such a post myself?

sentences.zh: 其學以誠敬為主，夜必就榻而後脫巾，旦必巾而後起。

translations.literal: His learning took sincerity and reverence as its foundation; at night he had to reach the couch before removing his headcloth, and in the morning he had to put on the headcloth before rising.
translations.idiomatic: His learning centered on sincerity and reverence: at night he would not remove his cap until he reached his bed; in the morning he would not rise until he had put it on.

sentences.zh: 居無惰容，喜無戲言，不事緣飾，不苟臧否。

translations.literal: At rest he had no lazy bearing, in joy no playful words; he did not pursue ornament, and did not lightly praise or blame.
translations.idiomatic: He never looked idle at home or spoke frivolously in mirth; he shunned ornament and never judged others lightly.

sentences.zh: 聞人片善，記其姓名。

translations.literal: When he heard the slightest good in a person he recorded his name.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the slightest good in someone, he would note the person's name.

sentences.zh: 遇饑凍者，推食解衣不靳。

translations.literal: When he met those hungry or freezing he shared food and stripped off clothing without stint.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting the hungry or cold, he shared food and gave away clothing without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 僦屋以居，未嘗戚戚。

translations.literal: He rented a house to live in and never once looked troubled.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in rented rooms and never showed distress.

sentences.zh: 尤袤為守，聞其名，遣書禮之。

translations.literal: You Mao was prefect and, hearing his name, sent a letter to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: When You Mao became prefect he heard of Tingyun and sent a letter of respect.

sentences.zh: 一日，巾車曆訪舊遊，徜徉幾月。

translations.literal: One day he took a covered carriage and visited old haunts, roaming for several months.
translations.idiomatic: One day he rode out in a covered carriage to revisit old places and wandered for months.

sentences.zh: 歸感微疾，端坐瞑目而逝，年八十有五。

translations.literal: On returning he felt a slight illness, sat upright with eyes closed and passed away, aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home, fell slightly ill, sat upright with closed eyes, and died at eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 鄉人崇敬之，以其父子俱隱遁，稱之曰二徐先生。

translations.literal: The people of the district revered them; because father and son both lived in reclusion they were called the Two Masters Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors revered them; because father and son both lived in seclusion they were called the Two Masters Xu.

sentences.zh: 淳熙間，常平使者朱熹行部，拜墓下，題詩有“道學傳千古，東甌說二徐”之句，且大書以表之曰“有宋高士二徐先生之墓”。

translations.literal: In the Chunxi era the Ever-Normal Granary commissioner Zhu Xi made a tour of the circuit, bowed at the tomb, and inscribed a poem with the lines "The learning of the Way is transmitted for a thousand ages; in Eastern Ou they speak of the Two Xu," and also wrote large characters to mark it, saying "Tomb of the Two Masters Xu, lofty scholars of the Song."
translations.idiomatic: During Chunxi, Zhu Xi as circuit commissioner visited their tomb and wrote a poem including the lines "The Way's learning endures a thousand years; in Eastern Ou they tell of the Two Xu," and inscribed a large tablet: "Tomb of the Two Xu, lofty scholars of Song."

sentences.zh: 庭筠之兄庭槐、庭蘭，皆有父風。

translations.literal: Tingyun's elder brothers Tinghuai and Tinglan both had their father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyun's elder brothers Tinghuai and Tinglan both bore their father's character.

sentences.zh: 孫日升，苦學有守，於是徐氏詩書不絕六世矣。

translations.literal: His grandson Risheng studied bitterly and had integrity; thus the Xu family's poetry and learning did not cease for six generations.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Risheng studied hard and held firm principles, and the Xu line of learning continued unbroken for six generations.

sentences.zh: 蘇雲卿，廣漢人。

translations.literal: Su Yunqing was a man of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yunqing was from Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 紹興間，來豫章東湖，結廬獨居。

translations.literal: In the Shaoxing era he came to the Eastern Lake of Yuzhang and built a hut to live alone.
translations.idiomatic: During Shaoxing he came to the Eastern Lake at Yuzhang and built a solitary hut.

sentences.zh: 待鄰曲有恩禮，無良賤老稚皆愛敬之，稱曰蘇翁。

translations.literal: In treating neighbors he had kindness and courtesy; whether worthy or base, old or young, all loved and respected him and called him Old Su.
translations.idiomatic: He treated neighbors with kindness; young and old, high and low alike loved and respected him and called him Old Su.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺，美須髯，寡言笑，布褐草履，終歲不易，未嚐疾病。

translations.literal: His body was seven feet tall, his beard and whiskers handsome; he spoke little and laughed little, wore hemp cloth and straw sandals unchanged through the year, and never suffered illness.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven feet tall with a fine beard, spoke and laughed little, wore the same hemp robe and straw sandals year-round, and was never ill.

sentences.zh: 披荊畚礫為圃，藝植耘芟，灌溉培壅，皆有法度。

translations.literal: He cleared brambles and carried basketloads of rubble to make a garden; planting, hoeing, weeding, irrigating, and mounding all had their methods.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared brambles and stones for a garden plot; planting, hoeing, weeding, watering, and mounding all followed fixed methods.

sentences.zh: 雖隆暑極寒，土焦草凍，圃不絕蔬，滋鬱暢茂，四時之品無闕者。

translations.literal: Though in extreme heat the soil scorched and in extreme cold the grass froze, the garden never lacked vegetables; lush and flourishing, the produce of the four seasons was never wanting.
translations.idiomatic: Even in scorching summer or freezing winter his plot never lacked vegetables; lush growth filled every season.

sentences.zh: 味視他圃尤勝，又不二價，市鬻者利倍而售速，先期輸直。

translations.literal: The flavor was superior to other gardens, and he did not charge two prices; those who sold at market doubled their profit and sold quickly, paying him in advance.
translations.idiomatic: His produce tasted better than others'; he never haggled, and vendors doubled their profit and sold fast, paying him in advance.

sentences.zh: 夜織屨，堅韌過革舄，人爭貿之以饋遠。

translations.literal: At night he wove sandals tougher than leather shoes; people vied to buy them to send as gifts far away.
translations.idiomatic: At night he wove sandals tougher than leather shoes, which people competed to buy as gifts for distant friends.

sentences.zh: 以故薪米不乏，有羨則以周急應貸，假者負償，一不經意。

translations.literal: Thus fuel and grain were never lacking; when he had surplus he used it to relieve emergencies and answer loans; if borrowers failed to repay he paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: So he never lacked fuel or grain; surplus went to the needy, and he never minded when borrowers failed to repay.

sentences.zh: 溉園之隙，閉門高臥，或危坐終日，莫測識也。

translations.literal: In the intervals of watering the garden he shut his door and lay high on his couch, or sat upright all day; no one could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: Between watering rounds he shut his door to sleep or sat upright all day—no one could fathom his mind.

sentences.zh: 少與張浚為布衣交，浚為相，馳書函金幣屬豫章帥及漕曰：“餘鄉人蘇雲卿，管、樂流亞，遁跡湖海有年矣。

translations.literal: In youth he and Zhang Jun were friends as commoners; when Jun became chief minister he sent a hurried letter with gold and silks, entrusting the prefect of Yuzhang and the transport commissioner, saying, "My fellow townsman Su Yunqing is of the class of Guan Zhong and Yue Yi and has hidden his traces on lakes and seas for many years.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he and Zhang Jun were friends; when Jun became chief minister he wrote the Yuzhang prefect and transport commissioner with gold and silks: "My townsman Su Yunqing rivals Guan Zhong and Yue Yi in talent and has lived in seclusion on lakes and rivers for years.

sentences.zh: 近聞灌園東湖，其高風偉節，非折簡能屈，幸親造其廬，必為我致之。”

translations.literal: I have lately heard he tends a garden at the Eastern Lake; his lofty bearing and great integrity cannot be bent by a mere letter—I hope you will personally visit his hut and be sure to bring him to me.
translations.idiomatic: I hear he now gardens at the Eastern Lake; his lofty integrity cannot be summoned by letter alone—please visit his hut in person and bring him to me.

sentences.zh: 帥、漕密物色，曰：“此獨有灌園蘇翁，無雲卿也。”

translations.literal: The prefect and commissioner secretly searched and said, "Here there is only Old Su who tends a garden; there is no Yunqing."
translations.idiomatic: The prefect and commissioner searched in secret and said, "We find only Old Su the gardener—no Yunqing."

sentences.zh: 帥、漕乃屏騎從，更服為遊士，入其圃，翁運鋤不顧。

translations.literal: The prefect and commissioner then dismissed their mounted escort, changed clothes to appear as traveling scholars, entered his garden, and the old man wielded his hoe without looking up.
translations.idiomatic: They dismissed their escorts, dressed as wandering scholars, entered his garden, and the old man kept hoeing without a glance.

sentences.zh: 進而揖之，翁曰：“二客何從來耶？”

translations.literal: Advancing they bowed to him; the old man said, "From where have the two guests come?"
translations.idiomatic: They stepped forward and bowed; he said, "Where have you two come from?"

sentences.zh: 延入室，土銼竹幾，地無纖塵，案上有《西漢書》一冊。

translations.literal: He invited them into the room: earthen couch and bamboo table, the floor without a speck of dust, and on the desk one volume of the History of the Western Han.
translations.idiomatic: He led them inside: an earthen couch, a bamboo table, a spotless floor, and one volume of the History of the Western Han on the desk.

sentences.zh: 二客恍若自失，默計此為蘇雲卿也。

translations.literal: The two guests seemed suddenly to lose themselves, silently reckoning that this must be Su Yunqing.
translations.idiomatic: The two men were struck dumb, silently sure this was Su Yunqing.

sentences.zh: 既而汲泉煮茗，意稍款浹，遂扣其鄉里，徐曰：“廣漢。”

translations.literal: Presently they drew spring water and brewed tea; their mood grew somewhat warm, and they asked his native place; he said slowly, "Guanghan."
translations.idiomatic: They drew spring water and brewed tea; as the mood warmed they asked his home; he answered slowly, "Guanghan."

sentences.zh: 客曰：“張德遠廣漢人，翁當識之。”

translations.literal: The guests said, "Zhang Deyuan is a man of Guanghan; the old man must know him."
translations.idiomatic: They said, "Zhang Deyuan is from Guanghan—you must know him."

translations.literal: He said, "Indeed."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I do."

sentences.zh: 客又問：“德遠何如人？”

translations.literal: The guests again asked, "What sort of man is Deyuan?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked, "What kind of man is Deyuan?"

sentences.zh: 曰：“賢人也。

translations.literal: He said, "A worthy man.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "A worthy man.

sentences.zh: 第長於知君子，短於知小人，德有餘而才不足。”

translations.literal: Only he is long in knowing gentlemen and short in knowing petty men; his virtue has surplus but his talent is insufficient."
translations.idiomatic: He is good at recognizing gentlemen but poor at spotting petty men—more virtue than talent."

sentences.zh: 因問：“德遠今何官？”

translations.literal: They then asked, "What office does Deyuan hold now?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked what office Deyuan held now.

sentences.zh: 二客曰：“今朝廷起張公，欲了此事。”

translations.literal: The two guests said, "Now the court has raised Lord Zhang, wishing to settle this affair."
translations.idiomatic: They said, "The court has recalled Lord Zhang to settle this matter."

sentences.zh: 翁曰：“此恐怕他未便了得在。”

translations.literal: The old man said, "I fear he may not yet be able to settle it."
translations.idiomatic: The old man said, "I'm afraid he may not be able to finish it yet."

sentences.zh: 二客起而言曰：“張公令某等致公，共濟大業。”

translations.literal: The two guests rose and said, "Lord Zhang ordered us to bring the old gentleman to join in accomplishing the great enterprise."
translations.idiomatic: They rose and said, "Lord Zhang sent us to invite you to help accomplish the great task."

sentences.zh: 因出書函金幣置幾上。

translations.literal: Thereupon they produced the letter and gold and silks and set them on the table.
translations.idiomatic: They laid out the letter and gold and silks on the table.

sentences.zh: 雲卿鼻間隱隱作聲，若自咎歎者。

translations.literal: Yunqing made a faint sound in his nose, as if sighing in self-reproach.
translations.idiomatic: Yunqing made a faint sound through his nose, as if sighing at himself.

sentences.zh: 二客力請共載，辭不可，期以詰朝上謁。

translations.literal: The two guests pressed him strongly to ride together; he declined and could not be moved, agreeing to call on them the next morning.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed him to ride with them; he refused and promised to call the next morning.

sentences.zh: 旦遣使迎伺，則扃戶闃然，排闥入，則書幣不啟，家具如故，而翁已遁矣，竟不知所往。

translations.literal: At dawn they sent men to wait and welcome him; the door was barred and still, they pushed it open and entered—the letter and gifts were unopened, the furnishings as before, but the old man had fled, and in the end no one knew where he had gone.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they sent men to fetch him; the door was barred and silent. They forced it open—the letter and gifts untouched, furniture unchanged—but the old man had vanished, and no one ever learned where he went.

sentences.zh: 帥、漕復命，浚拊幾歎曰：“求之不早，實懷竊位之羞。”

translations.literal: The prefect and commissioner reported back; Jun struck the table and sighed, "I did not seek him early—truly I feel the shame of holding office unworthily."
translations.idiomatic: When they reported back, Jun struck the table and sighed, "I sought him too late—I am ashamed to hold office unworthily."

sentences.zh: 作箴以識之，曰：“雲卿風節，高於傅霖。

translations.literal: He composed an admonition to record it, saying, "Yunqing's bearing and integrity are higher than Fu Lin's.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote an admonition in remembrance: "Yunqing's integrity surpasses Fu Lin's.

sentences.zh: 予期與之，共濟當今。

translations.literal: I hoped to join with him in saving the present age.
translations.idiomatic: I hoped to join him in saving the age.

sentences.zh: 山潛水杳，邈不可尋。

translations.literal: Hidden in mountains, lost in waters—far off and impossible to seek.
translations.idiomatic: He hides in mountains and rivers, beyond all finding.

sentences.zh: 弗力弗早，予罪曷針。”

translations.literal: Not striving, not early—how can my fault be mended?
translations.idiomatic: For lack of effort and timeliness, what fault of mine can be mended?

sentences.zh: 譙定，字天授，涪陵人。

translations.literal: Qiao Ding, style name Tianshou, was a man of Fuling.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Ding, courtesy name Tianshou, was from Fuling.

sentences.zh: 少喜學佛，析其理歸於儒。

translations.literal: In youth he delighted in studying Buddhism and analyzed its principles back to Confucianism.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied Buddhism but analyzed its principles back toward Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 後學《易》於郭曩氏，自“見乃謂之象”一語以入。

translations.literal: Later he studied the Changes under the Guo Rang clan, entering through the single phrase "what is seen is then called an image."
translations.idiomatic: He later studied the Changes under the Guo Rang family, entering through the line "what is seen is then called an image."

sentences.zh: 郭曩氏者，世家南平，始祖在漢為嚴君平之師，世傳《易》學，蓋象數之學也。

translations.literal: The Guo Rang clan were a hereditary family of Nanping; their founding ancestor in Han was the teacher of Yan Junping, and they transmitted the learning of the Changes for generations—this was essentially the learning of images and numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The Guo Rang were a hereditary Nanping family whose founder in Han had been Yan Junping's teacher; for generations they transmitted Changes learning—the school of images and numbers.

sentences.zh: 定一日至汴，聞伊川程頤講道於洛，潔衣往見，棄其學而學焉。

translations.literal: One day Ding reached Bian, heard that Cheng Yi of Yichuan lectured on the Way in Luoyang, put on plain clothes and went to see him, abandoned his former learning and studied under him.
translations.idiomatic: One day in Bian he heard that Cheng Yi of Yichuan was teaching in Luoyang; he went in plain dress, abandoned his old studies, and became Yi's student.

sentences.zh: 遂得聞精義，造詣愈至，浩然而歸。

translations.literal: He then heard the subtle meanings, his attainment grew ever deeper, and he returned in vast serenity.
translations.idiomatic: He grasped the subtle meanings, his attainment deepened, and he returned home in expansive calm.

sentences.zh: 其後頤貶涪，實定之鄉也，北山有岩，師友遊泳其中，涪人名之曰讀易洞。

translations.literal: Later Yi was banished to Fu—which was in fact Ding's home country; on the northern mountain was a grotto where teacher and friends roamed and bathed in study, and the people of Fu named it the Grotto for Reading the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi was later exiled to Fu—Ding's homeland—a grotto on the northern mountain where teacher and friends gathered was named the Grotto for Reading the Changes.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，呂好問薦之，欽宗召為崇政殿說書，以論弗合，辭不就。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang, Lü Haowen recommended him; Emperor Qinzong summoned him as lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, but because his discourse did not accord he declined and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingkang, Lü Haowen recommended him; Emperor Qinzong summoned him as Chongzheng Hall lecturer, but he declined when their views did not align.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，定猶在汴，右丞許翰又薦之，詔宗澤津遣詣行在。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, Ding was still in Bian; the Right Vice Director Xu Han again recommended him, and an edict ordered Zong Ze to escort him by ferry to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong acceded, Ding was still in Bian; Vice Director Xu Han recommended him again, and an edict ordered Zong Ze to ferry him to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 至惟揚，寓邸舍，窶甚，一中貴人偶與鄰，饋之食不受，與之衣亦不受，委金而去，定袖而歸之，其自立之操類此。

translations.literal: On reaching Weiyang he lodged in a hostel, extremely destitute; a palace eunuch happened to be a neighbor, offered him food which he would not accept, gave him clothes which he also would not accept, left gold and departed—Ding tucked it in his sleeve and returned it; his self-reliant integrity was of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: At Weiyang he lodged in an inn in deep poverty; a palace eunuch happened to be next door, offered food and clothing which he refused, and left gold—which Ding tucked in his sleeve and returned. His self-reliance was always thus.

sentences.zh: 上將用之，會金兵至，失定所在。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to employ him when the Jin army arrived and Ding's whereabouts were lost.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to employ him when Jin troops arrived and Ding disappeared.

sentences.zh: 復歸蜀，愛青城大麵之勝，棲遁其中，蜀人指其地曰譙岩。

translations.literal: He returned again to Shu, loved the excellence of Qingcheng and Damian, and dwelt in reclusion there; the people of Shu pointed to the place and called it Qiao Cliff.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Shu, loved the scenery of Qingcheng and Mount Damian, and lived in seclusion there; locals called the place Qiao Cliff.

sentences.zh: 敬定而不敢名，稱之曰譙夫子，有繪像祀之者，久而不衰。

translations.literal: They revered Ding but did not dare speak his name, calling him Master Qiao; some painted his image to sacrifice to him, and this did not fade for long.
translations.idiomatic: They revered him but did not speak his name, calling him Master Qiao; painted images were offered in worship for generations.

sentences.zh: 定《易》學得之程頤，授之胡憲、劉勉之，而馮時行、張行成則得定之餘意者也。

translations.literal: Ding's learning of the Changes he obtained from Cheng Yi and transmitted to Hu Xian and Liu Mianzhi; Feng Shixing and Zhang Xingcheng received the remainder of Ding's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Ding received his Changes learning from Cheng Yi and passed it to Hu Xian and Liu Mianzhi; Feng Shixing and Zhang Xingcheng received what remained of his teaching.

sentences.zh: 定後不知所終，樵夫牧童往往有見之者，世傳其為仙雲。

translations.literal: Afterward no one knew where Ding ended; woodcutters and herd boys often saw him, and the age transmitted that he had become an immortal.
translations.idiomatic: No one knew his final fate; woodcutters and herdboys often claimed to see him, and legend held he had become an immortal.

sentences.zh: 初，程頤之父向嚐守廣漢，頤與兄顥皆隨侍，遊成都，見治篾箍桶者挾冊，就視之則《易》也，欲擬議致詰，而篾者先曰：“若嚐學此乎？”

translations.literal: Earlier, Cheng Yi's father Xiang had once been prefect of Guanghan; Yi and his elder brother Hao both followed in attendance, traveled to Chengdu, and saw a man who mended bamboo and bound tubs carrying a book—going to look, it was the Changes; they wished to discuss and question him, but the bamboo-worker spoke first: "Have you studied this?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yi's father Xiang was prefect of Guanghan, Yi and his brother Hao accompanied him to Chengdu and saw a bamboo-worker carrying a book—it was the Changes. They were about to question him when the man spoke first: "Have you studied this?"

sentences.zh: 因指“《未濟》男之窮”以發問。

translations.literal: He then pointed to "the male's extremity in Wei Ji" to raise a question.
translations.idiomatic: He cited the line on "the male's extremity in Not Yet Fulfilled" to test them.

sentences.zh: 二程遜而問之，則曰：“三陽皆失位。”

translations.literal: The two Chengs yielded and questioned him; he said, "The three yang lines all lose their positions."
translations.idiomatic: The brothers humbly asked; he said, "All three yang lines have lost their proper places."

sentences.zh: 兄弟渙然有所省，翌日再過之，則去矣。

translations.literal: The brothers were suddenly enlightened; the next day they went again, but he had gone.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were suddenly enlightened; when they returned the next day he was gone.

sentences.zh: 其後袁滋入洛，問《易》於頤，頤曰：“《易》學在蜀耳，盍往求之？”

translations.literal: Later Yuan Zi entered Luoyang and asked Yi about the Changes; Yi said, "The learning of the Changes is in Shu—why not go seek it?"
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuan Zi came to Luoyang and asked Yi about the Changes; Yi said, "Changes learning is in Shu—why not go seek it there?"

sentences.zh: 滋入蜀訪問，久無所遇。

translations.literal: Zi entered Shu to inquire and search, and for a long time met with nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Zi went to Shu to seek him but for a long time found nothing.

sentences.zh: 已而見賣醬薛翁於眉、邛間，與語，大有所得，不知所得何語也。

translations.literal: Presently he saw Old Xue who sold sauce between Mei and Qiong, spoke with him, and gained greatly—what words he gained is not known.
translations.idiomatic: Later he met Old Xue the sauce-seller between Mei and Qiong; their talk brought him great insight, though what was said is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 憲、勉之、滋皆閩人，時行、行成蜀人，郭曩氏及篾叟、醬翁皆蜀之隱君子也。

translations.literal: Xian, Mianzhi, and Zi were all men of Min; Shixing and Xingcheng were men of Shu; the Guo Rang clan, the bamboo-worker, and the sauce-seller were all hidden gentlemen of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Xian, Liu Mianzhi, and Yuan Zi were from Fujian; Feng Shixing and Zhang Xingcheng from Sichuan; the Guo Rang family, the bamboo-worker, and the sauce-seller were all reclusive worthies of Shu.

sentences.zh: 王忠民，潁陽人，世業醫。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongmin was a man of Yingyang; his family profession for generations was medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongmin was from Yingyang; his family had practiced medicine for generations.

sentences.zh: 忠民幼通經史，自靖康以來，數言邊方利害於朝，累召弗至。

translations.literal: Zhongmin in youth mastered the classics and histories; from Jingkang onward he repeatedly spoke to the court of the advantages and harms on the frontier, and though summoned many times he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmin mastered the classics and histories in youth; from Jingkang on he repeatedly advised the court on frontier affairs, but though summoned many times he never came.

sentences.zh: 高宗渡江，忠民隱居不出，諸鎮翟興等皆重之，弗能致；

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong crossed the Yangzi, Zhongmin lived in seclusion and did not emerge; the various garrison commanders such as Zhai Xing all esteemed him but could not bring him in;
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong crossed the Yangzi, Zhongmin stayed in seclusion; garrison commanders such as Zhai Xing all esteemed him but could not win him out;

sentences.zh: 張浚授以迪功郎，不受。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun granted him the title of Diligent Merit Gentleman, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun offered him the rank of Diligent Merit Gentleman, which he refused.

sentences.zh: 興徙治藥川，忠民避地南下，遇商虢鎮撫使董先於內鄉，留軍中，事以師禮。

translations.literal: When Xing moved his administration to Yaochuan, Zhongmin fled south and met Dong Xian, pacification commissioner of Shang and Guo, at Neixiang; he remained in the army and was treated with the rites due a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: When Xing moved to Yaochuan, Zhongmin fled south, met Dong Xian the Shang-Guo pacification commissioner at Neixiang, joined his army, and was honored as a teacher.

sentences.zh: 時劉豫僭立，忠民作《九思圖》及定亂四象達之金主，及鏤板印圖散於偽境，以明天下之義。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yu usurped the throne; Zhongmin made the Diagram of Nine Reflections and the Four Images for Settling Disorder and sent them to the Jin ruler, and also carved blocks to print the diagrams and spread them through the false realm, to clarify the righteousness of All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu usurped the throne, Zhongmin composed the Diagram of Nine Reflections and the Four Images for Settling Disorder and sent them to the Jin ruler, printing and distributing them through the puppet state to proclaim the moral order of the realm.

sentences.zh: 紹興三年，翟琮薦其忠節於朝，特授宣教郎，詔董先津遣詣行在。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaoxing, Zhai Cong recommended his loyalty and integrity to the court; he was specially granted the title of Instruction Gentleman, and an edict ordered Dong Xian to ferry him to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing year 3, Zhai Cong recommended his loyalty; the court specially appointed him Instruction Gentleman and ordered Dong Xian to ferry him to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 既至，宰相呂頤浩、簽書樞密院事徐俯見之皆拜，舍於政府。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the chief minister Lü Yihao and the Secretariat drafter of the Bureau of Military Affairs Xu Fu, on seeing him, all bowed and lodged him at the chief councilor's residence.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival, Chief Minister Lü Yihao and Military Affairs Secretariat drafter Xu Fu both bowed to him and lodged him at the chief councilor's residence.

sentences.zh: 忠民上疏辭官，言：“臣憤金人無道，故三上金主書，乞還二帝，本心報國，非冀名祿。”

translations.literal: Zhongmin submitted a memorial declining office, saying, "Your servant resents the Jin people's lack of the Way; therefore I thrice sent letters to the Jin ruler begging the return of the two emperors. My original heart was to repay the state, not to hope for fame and stipend."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmin memorialized to decline office: "I resent the Jin for their lawlessness and thrice wrote their ruler begging return of the two emperors. My heart was to serve the state, not to seek rank or reward."

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 忠民以誥置櫝中，藏七寶山下，力懇求去。

translations.literal: Zhongmin placed the patent of appointment in a casket and hid it beneath Mount Qibao, earnestly begging to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmin boxed his appointment patent, hid it under Mount Qibao, and urgently begged to depart.

sentences.zh: 復依董先軍中，遂不出。

translations.literal: He again relied on Dong Xian's army and in the end did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: He rejoined Dong Xian's army and never came out again.

sentences.zh: 時又有蘇庠者，丹陽人。

translations.literal: At that time there was also Su Kuang, a man of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Su Kuang of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 紳之後，頌之族也。

translations.literal: He was a descendant of Su Shen and of the clan of Su Song.
translations.idiomatic: He was descended from Su Shen and belonged to the clan of Su Song.

sentences.zh: 少能詩，蘇軾見其《清江曲》，大愛之，由是知名。

translations.literal: In youth he could compose poetry; Su Shi saw his "Song of the Clear River" and greatly loved it, and from this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote poetry in youth; Su Shi greatly admired his "Song of the Clear River," and he became famous thereby.

sentences.zh: 徐俯薦其賢，上特召之，固辭；

translations.literal: Xu Fu recommended his worth; the emperor specially summoned him, but he firmly declined;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fu recommended him; the emperor summoned him specially, but he firmly declined;

sentences.zh: 又命守臣以禮津遣，庠辭疾不至，以壽終。

translations.literal: again ordered the local officials to escort him by ferry with ceremony; Kuang declined on grounds of illness and did not come, and ended his life in longevity.
translations.idiomatic: the court again ordered local officials to escort him with ceremony; Kuang pleaded illness and never came, and died at an advanced age.

sentences.zh: 劉勉之，字致中，建州崇安人。

translations.literal: Liu Mianzhi, style name Zhizhong, was a man of Chong'an in Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mianzhi, courtesy name Zhizhong, was from Chong'an in Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 自幼強學，日誦數千言。

translations.literal: From childhood he studied strenuously, reciting several thousand words each day.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he studied hard, reciting several thousand characters a day.

sentences.zh: 踰冠，以鄉舉詣太學。

translations.literal: After reaching the capping age he went to the Imperial Academy on a village recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: After coming of age he entered the Imperial Academy on a local recommendation.

sentences.zh: 時蔡京用事，禁止毋得挾元祐書，自是伊、洛之學不行。

translations.literal: At that time Cai Jing held power and forbade carrying Yuanyou-era books; from this the learning of Yichuan and Luoyang was not practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing then held power and forbade possession of Yuanyou-era texts, so the Cheng-Zhang school ceased to circulate.

sentences.zh: 勉之求得其書，每深夜，同舍生皆寐，乃潛抄而默誦之。

translations.literal: Mianzhi sought and obtained these books; each deep night, when his dormitory mates all slept, he would secretly copy and silently recite them.
translations.idiomatic: Mianzhi obtained these books and, late each night when his roommates slept, secretly copied and memorized them.

sentences.zh: 譙定至京師，勉之聞其從程頤遊，邃《易》學，遂師事之。

translations.literal: When Qiao Ding reached the capital, Mianzhi heard that he had followed Cheng Yi in study and was deep in the learning of the Changes, and thereupon took him as master.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiao Ding came to the capital, Mianzhi heard he had studied under Cheng Yi and was deep in the Changes, and became his student.

sentences.zh: 已而厭科舉業，揖諸生歸，見劉安世、楊時，皆請業焉。

translations.literal: Presently he grew weary of examination studies, bowed to his fellow students and returned, met Liu Anshi and Yang Shi, and sought instruction from them all.
translations.idiomatic: He soon wearied of the examination curriculum, took leave of his classmates, and sought instruction from Liu Anshi and Yang Shi.

sentences.zh: 及至家，即邑近郊結草為堂，讀書其中，力耕自給，澹然無求於世。

translations.literal: When he reached home he at once built a hall of thatch on the outskirts of the district, read books within it, plowed strenuously to support himself, and was tranquil without seeking anything from the world.
translations.idiomatic: At home he built a thatched hall on the town outskirts, studied there, farmed to support himself, and lived without worldly ambition.

sentences.zh: 與胡憲、劉子翬相往來，日以講論切磋為事。

translations.literal: With Hu Xian and Liu Zihui he associated back and forth, taking daily discussion and mutual refinement as his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He associated with Hu Xian and Liu Zihui, devoting his days to discussion and mutual refinement.

sentences.zh: 紹興間，中書舍人呂本中疏其行義誌業以聞，特召詣闕。

translations.literal: In the Shaoxing era the Secretariat drafter Lü Benzhong memorialized his conduct, integrity, and purpose to inform the throne, and he was specially summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: During Shaoxing, Secretariat drafter Lü Benzhong reported his conduct and purpose, and he was specially summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 秦檜方主和，慮勉之見上持正論，乃不引見，但令策試後省給劄而已。

translations.literal: Qin Hui was then advocating peace and feared that if Mianzhi saw the emperor he would uphold upright discourse; therefore he was not granted audience but only ordered to take the policy examination of the rear secretariat and given a letter.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui, then advocating peace, feared Mianzhi would argue for a hard line before the emperor and refused him audience, ordering only a rear-secretariat examination.

sentences.zh: 勉之知不與檜合，即謝病歸。

translations.literal: Mianzhi knew he did not accord with Hui and at once pleaded illness and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not agree with Hui, Mianzhi pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 杜門十餘年，學者踵至，隨其材品，為說聖賢教學之門及前言往行之懿。

translations.literal: He shut his door for more than ten years; scholars came in succession, and according to their talent and character he expounded the gates of the sages' teaching and the excellence of former words and past conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his door closed for more than ten years while students flocked to him; he taught each according to ability, opening the way of the sages and the excellence of past exemplars.

sentences.zh: 所居有白水，人號曰白水先生。

translations.literal: Where he dwelt there was White Water, and people called him Master of White Water.
translations.idiomatic: A stream called White Water ran near his home, and people called him Master of White Water.

sentences.zh: 賢士大夫自趙鼎以下皆敬慕與交。

translations.literal: Worthy officials and gentlemen from Zhao Ding downward all revered and admired him and associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy officials from Zhao Ding downward all revered him and sought his friendship.

sentences.zh: 後秦檜益橫，鼎竄死，諸賢禁錮，勉之竟不復出。

translations.literal: Later Qin Hui grew ever more overbearing; Ding was driven to death in exile and worthy men were imprisoned; Mianzhi in the end never emerged again.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui grew more tyrannical, Zhao Ding died in exile, and worthy men were silenced, Mianzhi never emerged again.

sentences.zh: 勉之一介不妄取。

translations.literal: Mianzhi would not take a single thing unrightfully.
translations.idiomatic: Mianzhi would not take the slightest thing unrightfully.

sentences.zh: 婦家富，無子，謀盡以貲歸於女，勉之不受，以畀族之賢者，命之奉祀。

translations.literal: His wife's family was wealthy and had no son; they planned to give all their property to the daughter; Mianzhi would not accept it but gave it to a worthy man of the clan and ordered him to maintain the sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His wife's wealthy family, lacking a son, planned to leave all property to the daughter; Mianzhi refused it, gave it to a worthy clansman, and charged him with maintaining the ancestral sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 其友朱鬆卒，屬以後事，且戒其子熹受學。

translations.literal: When his friend Zhu Song died, he entrusted him with later affairs and also admonished his son Xi to receive learning.
translations.idiomatic: When his friend Zhu Song died, he entrusted him with his affairs and urged his son Xi to study under him.

sentences.zh: 勉之經理其家，而誨熹如子侄。

translations.literal: Mianzhi managed his household and instructed Xi as if he were a son or nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Mianzhi managed Zhu's household and taught Xi as he would a son or nephew.

sentences.zh: 熹之得道，自勉之始。

translations.literal: Xi's attaining the Way began with Mianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's path to the Way began with Mianzhi.

sentences.zh: 紹興十九年，卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Shaoxing he died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Shaoxing year 19, aged fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 胡憲，字原仲，居建之崇安。

translations.literal: Hu Xian, style name Yuanzhong, dwelt in Chong'an of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Xian, courtesy name Yuanzhong, lived in Chong'an, Jian.

sentences.zh: 生而靜愨，不妄笑語，長從從父胡安國學。

translations.literal: From birth he was quiet and sincere, not laughing or speaking lightly; growing up he followed his father's younger brother Hu Anguo in study.
translations.idiomatic: From birth he was quiet and sincere, never laughing or speaking lightly; he studied under his uncle Hu Anguo.

sentences.zh: 平居危坐植立，時然後言，雖倉卒無疾言遽色，人犯之未嚐校。

translations.literal: In ordinary life he sat upright and stood erect, speaking only when the time was right; even in haste he had no hurried words or sudden color, and when others offended him he never retaliated.
translations.idiomatic: In daily life he sat upright and spoke only when appropriate; even in haste he never spoke sharply, and when others offended him he never retaliated.

sentences.zh: 紹興中以鄉貢入太學。

translations.literal: In the Shaoxing era he entered the Imperial Academy on a village tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During Shaoxing he entered the Imperial Academy on a local tribute.

sentences.zh: 會伊、洛學有禁，憲獨陰與劉勉之誦習其說。

translations.literal: It happened that the learning of Yichuan and Luoyang was banned; Xian alone, in secret with Liu Mianzhi, recited and practiced its doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: When the Cheng-Zhang school was banned, Xian alone studied its doctrines in secret with Liu Mianzhi.

sentences.zh: 既而學《易》於譙定，久未有得，定曰：“心為物漬，故不能有見，唯學乃可明耳。”

translations.literal: Presently he studied the Changes under Qiao Ding; for long he had no attainment; Ding said, "The mind is soaked by things, therefore it cannot have insight—only through learning can it be illumined."
translations.idiomatic: He later studied the Changes under Qiao Ding but long made no progress; Ding said, "The mind is stained by things and cannot see clearly—only learning can illumine it."

sentences.zh: 憲喟然歎曰：“所謂學者，非克己工夫耶？”

translations.literal: Xian sighed deeply and said, "What is called learning—is it not the effort of overcoming the self?"
translations.idiomatic: Xian sighed and said, "Is not learning the work of self-discipline?"

sentences.zh: 自是一意下學，不求人知。

translations.literal: From this he single-mindedly applied himself to learning and did not seek that others know him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he devoted himself wholly to learning and sought no recognition.

sentences.zh: 一旦，揖諸生歸故山，力田賣藥，以奉其親。

translations.literal: One day he bowed to his fellow students and returned to his native hills, plowing strenuously and selling medicine to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: One day he took leave of his classmates, returned to his native hills, farmed and sold medicine to support his parents.

sentences.zh: 安國稱其有隱君子之操。

translations.literal: Anguo praised him as having the integrity of a hidden gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo praised his integrity as that of a true recluse.

sentences.zh: 從遊者日眾，號籍溪先生，賢士大夫亦高仰之。

translations.literal: Those who followed him in study grew daily; he was called Master of Jixi Creek, and worthy officials and gentlemen also looked up to him highly.
translations.idiomatic: Students flocked to him; he was called Master of Jixi Creek, and worthy officials held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 折彥質、範衝、朱震、劉子羽、呂祉、呂本中共以其行義聞於朝，上特召之，憲辭母老。

translations.literal: Zhe Yanzhi, Fan Chong, Zhu Zhen, Liu Ziyu, Lü Zhi, and Lü Benzhong together reported his conduct and integrity to the court; the emperor specially summoned him, and Xian declined on grounds that his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe Yanzhi, Fan Chong, Zhu Zhen, Liu Ziyu, Lü Zhi, and Lü Benzhong reported his conduct to court; the emperor summoned him, but Xian declined because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 及彥質入西府，又言於上，趣召愈急，憲力辭。

translations.literal: When Yanzhi entered the western bureau he again spoke to the emperor; the urgent summons grew ever more pressing, and Xian firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhi entered the western bureau he urged the emperor again; summons grew urgent, but Xian firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 乃賜進士出身，授左迪功郎、添差建州教授，憲猶不屈。

translations.literal: He was then granted jinshi status, appointed Left Diligent Merit Gentleman and additional-assignee professor of Jianzhou, but Xian still would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted jinshi status and appointed Left Diligent Merit Gentleman and additional professor at Jianzhou, but Xian still refused.

sentences.zh: 太守魏矼遣行義諸生入裏致詔，且為手書陳大義，開譬甚力，憲不得已就職。

translations.literal: The prefect Wei Kang sent worthy students of conduct into the village to deliver the edict, and also wrote by hand setting forth the great principle, exhorting with great force; Xian had no choice but to take office.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Wei Kang sent worthy students to deliver the edict and wrote personally urging him at length; Xian had no choice but to accept.

sentences.zh: 日與諸生接，訓以為己之學。

translations.literal: Daily he met with students and instructed them in learning for the self.
translations.idiomatic: Daily he taught students the learning of self-cultivation.

sentences.zh: 聞者始而笑，中而疑，久而觀其所以修身、事親、接人者，無一不如所言，遂翕然悅服。

translations.literal: Those who heard at first laughed, then came to doubt, but after long observation of how he cultivated himself, served parents, and met people—nothing was not as he had said—they thereupon united in joyful submission.
translations.idiomatic: Students first laughed, then doubted, but seeing how he cultivated himself, served his parents, and treated others—always as he taught—they came to submit wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 郡人程元以篤行稱，龔何以廉節著，皆迎致俾參學政，學者自是大化。

translations.literal: The district's Cheng Yuan was famed for steadfast conduct and Gong He for integrity; both were welcomed and caused to assist in academic administration, and from this scholars were greatly transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yuan was famed for steadfast conduct and Gong He for integrity; both were invited to assist in teaching, and students were greatly transformed.

sentences.zh: 因七年不徙官，以母年高不樂居官舍，求監南嶽廟以歸。

translations.literal: Because for seven years he was not transferred in office, and because his mother was advanced in years and disliked dwelling in official quarters, he sought to supervise the Southern Marchmount shrine and return home.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years without transfer, and because his elderly mother disliked official lodgings, he sought appointment as supervisor of the Southern Marchmount shrine and returned home.

sentences.zh: 久之，起為福建路安撫使司屬官。

translations.literal: After long delay he was raised to an aide in the Fujian Circuit Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed aide in the Fujian Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 時帥張宗元榷鹽急，私販者銖兩亦重坐。

translations.literal: At that time the commander Zhang Zongyuan was severe in salt monopoly; even private sellers of an ounce or two received heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Zhang Zongyuan enforced the salt monopoly harshly; even petty smugglers received heavy sentences.

sentences.zh: 憲告以為政大體，宗元不悅，憲復請祠而去。

translations.literal: Xian advised him on the great principles of governing; Zongyuan was displeased, and Xian again requested a shrine post and left.
translations.idiomatic: Xian advised him on the principles of governance; when Zongyuan took offense, Xian again sought a shrine appointment and left.

sentences.zh: 秦檜方用事，諸賢零落，憲家居不出。

translations.literal: Qin Hui was then in power; worthy men were scattered and fallen; Xian dwelt at home and did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: While Qin Hui held power and worthy men were driven out, Xian stayed home.

sentences.zh: 檜死，以大理司直召，未行，改秘書正字。

translations.literal: When Hui died he was summoned as rectifier of the Court of Judicial Review; before he set out it was changed to Secretariat corrector.
translations.idiomatic: After Hui's death he was summoned as Court of Judicial Review rectifier, then reassigned as Secretariat corrector before departing.

sentences.zh: 既至，次當奏事，而病不能朝，乃草疏言：“金人大治汴京宮室，勢必敗盟。

translations.literal: When he arrived his turn came to memorialize, but illness prevented court attendance; he thereupon drafted a memorial saying, "The Jin are greatly repairing the palaces of Bianjing and will surely break the treaty.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he was due to memorialize but fell too ill to attend court; he drafted a memorial: "The Jin are rebuilding Bianjing's palaces and will surely break the treaty.

sentences.zh: 今元臣、宿將惟張浚、劉錡在，識者皆謂金果南牧，非此兩人莫能當。

translations.literal: Now among senior ministers and veteran generals only Zhang Jun and Liu Qi remain; those with insight all say that if the Jin truly drive south to pasture, none but these two men can withstand them.
translations.idiomatic: Of senior ministers and veteran generals only Zhang Jun and Liu Qi remain; informed opinion holds that if the Jin invade south, only these two can resist.

sentences.zh: 願亟起之，臣死不恨。”

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will quickly raise them; your servant will die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that they be recalled at once; then I can die without regret.

sentences.zh: 時兩人皆為積毀所傷，未有敢顯言其當用者，憲獨首言之。

translations.literal: At that time both men had been wounded by accumulated slander, and none dared openly say they should be employed; Xian alone was first to speak it.
translations.idiomatic: Both had been damaged by accumulated slander, and none dared openly urge their recall; Xian alone spoke first.

sentences.zh: 疏入，即求去。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered he at once requested to leave.
translations.idiomatic: After submitting the memorial he immediately asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其忠，詔改秩與祠歸。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his loyalty and ordered a change of rank and a shrine appointment for his return.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his loyalty and granted him a higher rank and shrine appointment to return home.

sentences.zh: 初，憲與劉勉之俱隱，後又與劉子翬、朱鬆交。

translations.literal: Earlier Xian and Liu Mianzhi both lived in seclusion; later he also associated with Liu Zihui and Zhu Song.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xian and Liu Mianzhi had both lived in seclusion; he later befriended Liu Zihui and Zhu Song.

sentences.zh: 鬆將沒，屬其子熹受學於憲與勉之、子翬。

translations.literal: When Song was about to die he entrusted his son Xi to receive learning from Xian, Mianzhi, and Zihui.
translations.idiomatic: As Song lay dying he entrusted his son Xi to study under Xian, Mianzhi, and Zihui.

sentences.zh: 熹自謂從三君子遊，而事籍溪先生為久。

translations.literal: Xi himself said he had followed the three gentlemen in study but served Master of Jixi Creek the longest.
translations.idiomatic: Xi said he had studied with all three gentlemen but served Master of Jixi Creek longest.

sentences.zh: 方憲之以館職召也，適秦檜諱言之後，憲與王十朋、馮方、查籥、李浩相繼論事，太學士為《五賢詩》以歌之。

translations.literal: When Xian was summoned to a palace post, it happened to be after Qin Hui's taboo on speaking; Xian with Wang Shipeng, Feng Fang, Zha Yao, and Li Hao in succession discussed state affairs, and Imperial Academy students composed the "Poem of the Five Worthies" to sing them.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian was summoned to a palace post—just after Qin Hui's silencing of dissent—he joined Wang Shipeng, Feng Fang, Zha Yao, and Li Hao in speaking out; academy students composed the "Poem of the Five Worthies" in their honor.

sentences.zh: 人始信憲之不苟出，而惜其在位僅半年，不究其底蘊雲。

translations.literal: People then believed that Xian did not emerge from seclusion lightly, but regretted that in office he was barely half a year and did not plumb his full depth.
translations.idiomatic: People then understood he had not left seclusion lightly, but regretted that he held office barely half a year without fully realizing his potential.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十二年，卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Shaoxing he died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Shaoxing year 32, aged seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 郭雍，字子和，其先洛陽人。

translations.literal: Guo Yong, style name Zihe, his ancestors were men of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yong, courtesy name Zihe, was descended from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 父忠孝，官至太中大夫，師事程頤，著《易說》，號兼山先生，自有傳。

translations.literal: His father Zhongxiao reached office as Grandee of Palace Attendance, took Cheng Yi as teacher, wrote Explanations of the Changes, and was styled Master of Both Mountains—he has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guo Zhongxiao rose to Grandee of Palace Attendance, studied under Cheng Yi, wrote Explanations of the Changes, and was known as Master of Both Mountains—he has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 雍傳其父學，通世務，隱居峽州，放浪長楊山谷間，號白雲先生。

translations.literal: Yong transmitted his father's learning, understood worldly affairs, lived in seclusion in Xiazhou, wandered freely in the Changyang valleys, and was styled Master of White Cloud.
translations.idiomatic: Yong inherited his father's learning, understood worldly affairs, lived in seclusion in Xiazhou, wandered the Changyang valleys, and was known as Master of White Cloud.

sentences.zh: 乾道中，以峽守任清臣、湖北帥張孝祥薦於朝，旌召不起，賜號衝晦處士。

translations.literal: In the Qiandao era the Xiazhou prefect Ren Qingchen and the Hubei commander Zhang Xiaoxiang recommended him to court; the imperial summons he did not answer, and he was granted the style Reclusive Gentleman of Hidden Brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: During Qiandao, Xiazhou prefect Ren Qingchen and Hubei commander Zhang Xiaoxiang recommended him; he declined the imperial summons and was granted the title Reclusive Gentleman of Hidden Brilliance.

sentences.zh: 孝宗稔知其賢，每對輔臣稱道之，命所在州郡歲時致禮存問。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong was well aware of his worth; whenever he faced his assisting ministers he praised him and ordered the prefectures where he dwelt to send seasonal courtesy and inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong knew his worth well, praised him to his ministers, and ordered local prefectures to send seasonal greetings.

sentences.zh: 後更封頤正先生，令部使者遣官就問雍所欲言，備錄繳進。

translations.literal: Later he was further enfeoffed as Master of Nourishing Rectitude, and circuit envoys were ordered to send officials to ask what Yong wished to say and record it fully for submission.
translations.idiomatic: He was later ennobled as Master of Nourishing Rectitude; circuit envoys were ordered to record whatever Yong wished to say and submit it to court.

sentences.zh: 於是，雍年八十有三矣。

translations.literal: At this time Yong was eighty-three years old.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yong was eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 淳熙初，學者裒集程顥、程頤、張載、遊酢、楊時及忠孝、雍凡七家，為《大易粹言》行於世。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunxi scholars collected Cheng Hao, Cheng Yi, Zhang Zai, You Zuo, Yang Shi, and Zhongxiao and Yong—seven houses in all—and made Great Purified Words on the Changes, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chunxi scholars collected the works of Cheng Hao, Cheng Yi, Zhang Zai, You Zuo, Yang Shi, Guo Zhongxiao, and Guo Yong—seven masters—and published Great Purified Words on the Changes.

sentences.zh: 其述雍之說曰：

translations.literal: Their account of Yong's doctrines says:
translations.idiomatic: Their account of Yong's teaching runs:

sentences.zh: 《易》貫通三才，包括萬理。

translations.literal: The Changes penetrate the three powers and embrace the myriad principles.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes penetrate heaven, earth, and humanity and embrace all principles.

sentences.zh: 伏羲氏之畫，得於天而明天。

translations.literal: The diagrams of Fuxi obtained from Heaven and illumined Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxi's trigrams derived from Heaven and illumined Heaven.

sentences.zh: 文王之畫，得於人而明人。

translations.literal: The diagrams of King Wen obtained from humanity and illumined humanity.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen's hexagrams derived from humanity and illumined humanity.

sentences.zh: 羲畫為天，天，君道也，故五之在人為君。

translations.literal: Fuxi's diagrams are Heaven; Heaven is the way of the ruler; therefore the fifth line in humanity is the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxi's diagrams represent Heaven; Heaven is the way of the ruler; hence the fifth line in human affairs stands for the ruler.

sentences.zh: 文重為地，地，臣道也，故二之在人為臣。

translations.literal: Wen's lower trigram is Earth; Earth is the way of the minister; therefore the second line in humanity is the minister.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's lower trigram represents Earth; Earth is the way of the minister; hence the second line stands for the minister.

sentences.zh: 以上下二卦別而言之如此。

translations.literal: Speaking separately of the upper and lower trigrams, it is thus.
translations.idiomatic: This is how the upper and lower trigrams are to be understood separately.

sentences.zh: 合六爻而言之，則三四皆人道也，故謂之中爻。

translations.literal: Speaking of the six lines together, the third and fourth are both the way of humanity; therefore they are called the central lines.
translations.idiomatic: Taken together, the third and fourth lines both represent the human way and are called the central lines.

sentences.zh: 《乾》，元亨利貞，初曰四德。

translations.literal: In Qian—origination, penetration, benefit, and correctness—the beginning speaks of the four virtues.
translations.idiomatic: In Qian—origination, penetration, benefit, and correctness—the text first names the four virtues.

sentences.zh: 後又曰乾元，始而亨者也。

translations.literal: Later it again says "Qian origination"—origination and then penetration.
translations.idiomatic: Later it says "Qian origination"—origination followed by penetration.

sentences.zh: 利牝馬貞，利君子貞。

translations.literal: "Benefit the mare's correctness; benefit the gentleman's correctness."
translations.idiomatic: "Benefit the mare's correctness; benefit the gentleman's correctness."

sentences.zh: 是以四德為二義亦可矣。

translations.literal: Thus the four virtues may also be taken as two meanings.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the four virtues may also be understood as two meanings.

sentences.zh: 乾，陽物也。

translations.literal: Qian is the yang thing.
translations.idiomatic: Qian is the yang principle.

sentences.zh: 坤，陰物也。

translations.literal: Kun is the yin thing.
translations.idiomatic: Kun is the yin principle.

sentences.zh: 由《乾》一卦論之，則元與亨陽之類，利與貞陰之類也。

translations.literal: Considering from the single hexagram Qian, then origination and penetration belong to the yang class, benefit and correctness to the yin class.
translations.idiomatic: From the hexagram Qian alone, origination and penetration belong to yang, benefit and correctness to yin.

sentences.zh: 是猶春夏秋冬雖為四時，由陰陽觀之，則春夏為陽，秋冬為陰也。

translations.literal: This is like spring, summer, autumn, and winter—though they are four seasons, viewed through yin and yang, spring and summer are yang and autumn and winter are yin.
translations.idiomatic: It is like the four seasons: spring and summer are yang, autumn and winter yin.

sentences.zh: 天之所謂元亨利貞者，如立天之道，陰與陽之類也。

translations.literal: What Heaven calls origination, penetration, benefit, and correctness is like establishing Heaven's Way—the classes of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's origination, penetration, benefit, and correctness are like establishing Heaven's Way—the categories of yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 地之所謂元亨利貞者，如立地之道，柔與剛之類也。

translations.literal: What Earth calls origination, penetration, benefit, and correctness is like establishing Earth's Way—the classes of yielding and firm.
translations.idiomatic: Earth's four virtues are like establishing Earth's Way—the categories of yielding and firm.

sentences.zh: 人之所謂元亨利貞者，如立人之道，仁與義之類也。

translations.literal: What humanity calls origination, penetration, benefit, and correctness is like establishing humanity's Way—the classes of benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Humanity's four virtues are like establishing the human Way—the categories of benevolence and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 又《坤》之六五，坤雖臣道，五實君位，雖以柔德，不害其為君；

translations.literal: Again, the sixth line of Kun: though Kun is the way of the minister, the fifth position is in fact the ruler's place; though with yielding virtue, this does not harm its being ruler;
translations.idiomatic: In Kun's sixth line, though Kun is the minister's way, the fifth position is truly the ruler's; yielding virtue does not prevent its being sovereign;

sentences.zh: 猶《乾》之九二，雖有君德，不害其為臣。

translations.literal: just as the second line of Qian, though it has ruler's virtue, does not harm its being minister.
translations.idiomatic: just as Qian's second line, though bearing ruler's virtue, remains the minister's position.

sentences.zh: 故乾有兩君，德無兩君；

translations.literal: Therefore Qian has two rulers in position, but in virtue there are not two rulers;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Qian has two ruler-positions, but only one ruler in virtue;

sentences.zh: 坤有兩臣，德無兩臣。

translations.literal: Kun has two ministers in position, but in virtue there are not two ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Kun has two minister-positions, but only one minister in virtue.

sentences.zh: 六五以柔居尊，下下之君也。

translations.literal: The sixth line, with yielding virtue dwelling in honor, is a ruler who lowers himself below others.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth line, yielding yet honored, is the ruler who humbles himself below others.

sentences.zh: 江海所以能為百穀王者，以其善下下也。

translations.literal: Rivers and seas can be kings of the hundred valleys because they are good at placing themselves below.
translations.idiomatic: Rivers and seas rule the hundred valleys because they place themselves below.

sentences.zh: 下下本坤德也。

translations.literal: Lowering oneself below others is fundamentally Kun's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Humbling oneself is Kun's essential virtue.

sentences.zh: 黃，中色也，色之至美也；

translations.literal: Yellow is the central color, the most beautiful of colors;
translations.idiomatic: Yellow is the central color, the finest of colors;

sentences.zh: 裳，下服也，是以至美之德而下人也。

translations.literal: the lower garment is lower dress; thus with the most beautiful virtue one lowers oneself before others.
translations.idiomatic: the lower garment is humble dress—thus the finest virtue humbles itself before others.

sentences.zh: 其發明精到如此。

translations.literal: His elucidations were so penetrating and precise.
translations.idiomatic: His expositions were as penetrating and precise as this.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十四年。

translations.literal: The fourteenth year of Chunxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Chunxi,

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: he died.
translations.idiomatic: he died.

sentences.zh: 劉愚，字必明，衢州龍遊人。

translations.literal: Liu Yu, style name Biming, was a man of Longyou in Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, courtesy name Biming, was from Longyou in Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼警敏力學。

translations.literal: In youth he was alert and keen and studied strenuously.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was quick-witted and studied hard.

sentences.zh: 弱冠入太學，有聲，受業者甚眾。

translations.literal: At the capping age he entered the Imperial Academy, gained a reputation, and had very many who received his instruction.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he entered the Imperial Academy, won renown, and drew many students.

sentences.zh: 侍御史柴瑾、祭酒顏師魯、博士林光朝深器重之。

translations.literal: The attendant censor Chai Jin, the libationer Yan Shilu, and the erudite Lin Guangchao deeply valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant censor Chai Jin, libationer Yan Shilu, and erudite Lin Guangchao held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 瑾每奏對稱上意，則曰：“臣客劉愚為臣言。”

translations.literal: Whenever Jin's memorial responses pleased the emperor, he would say, "Your servant's guest Liu Yu spoke thus to your servant."
translations.idiomatic: When Jin's answers pleased the emperor, he would say, "My guest Liu Yu advised me thus."

sentences.zh: 師魯嚐奏愚行藝，上記曰：“此向者柴瑾所薦也。”

translations.literal: Shilu once memorialized Yu's conduct and learning; the emperor noted, "This is the one Chai Jin recommended before."
translations.idiomatic: Shilu once reported Yu's conduct; the emperor noted, "This is the man Chai Jin recommended earlier."

sentences.zh: 上舍釋褐，居第一。

translations.literal: When the upper dormitory was released from student status, he ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: When the upper dormitory graduated, he ranked first.

sentences.zh: 調江陵府教授，早晚為諸生講說，同僚相率以聽。

translations.literal: He was assigned as professor of Jiangling prefecture, lecturing morning and evening to students; his colleagues all followed to listen.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned professor at Jiangling, he lectured morning and evening; colleagues flocked to hear him.

sentences.zh: 愚益謙下，與葉適、項安世講論不倦，每以隱居學道為樂。

translations.literal: Yu grew ever more humble, discussed tirelessly with Ye Shi and Xiang Anshi, and took joy in living in seclusion and studying the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Yu grew humbler still, debated tirelessly with Ye Shi and Xiang Anshi, and found joy in seclusion and learning.

sentences.zh: 歲滿，帥王藺致書剡辟，固辭，貧不能歸。

translations.literal: When his term ended, the commander Wang Lin sent a letter to recruit him by imperial order; he firmly declined and was too poor to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, commander Wang Lin recruited him by edict; he refused and was too poor to go home.

sentences.zh: 外移安鄉縣令，邑逋賦萬計，愚核實數，寬限期，民不見吏而賦自足。

translations.literal: He was transferred outward to be magistrate of Anxiang county; the district's arrears in tax numbered in the tens of thousands; Yu verified the true figures, extended deadlines, and the people never saw an official yet the taxes were fully paid.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Anxiang as magistrate, he found tax arrears in the tens of thousands; he verified figures, extended deadlines, and collections were complete without harassing the people.

sentences.zh: 會歲歉，出常平米振貸，邑佐持不可，愚曰：“有罪不以相累。”

translations.literal: It happened to be a lean year; he released Ever-Normal Granary rice for relief loans; the county aide objected that it could not be done; Yu said, "If there is guilt, do not implicate one another."
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year he released Ever-Normal Granary grain for relief; when aides objected, Yu said, "If there is blame, let it not fall on you."

sentences.zh: 出緡錢數千萬，召商糴他郡而收元直，米價頓平，猶積廩數千石以備饑旱。

translations.literal: He issued several tens of millions in cash, summoned merchants to purchase grain in other prefectures and collected the original price; grain prices immediately stabilized, and he still accumulated several thousand bushels in granaries against famine and drought.
translations.idiomatic: He spent tens of millions in cash, summoned merchants to buy grain elsewhere at fair price, stabilized prices, and stockpiled thousands of bushels against future famine.

sentences.zh: 邑有範仲淹讀書地，為繪像立祠，興學，士競知勸。

translations.literal: The district had Fan Zhongyan's place of study; he painted his image and established a shrine, promoted learning, and scholars competed in encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Where Fan Zhongyan had studied, he erected a portrait-shrine, promoted schools, and scholars vied to emulate him.

sentences.zh: 諸司交薦，改秩，愚雅不樂仕進，遂致仕。

translations.literal: Various offices recommended him in turn; his rank was changed, but Yu by nature did not delight in advancing in office and thereupon retired.
translations.idiomatic: Offices recommended him and his rank was raised, but Yu disliked advancement and retired.

sentences.zh: 丞相餘端禮，鄉人也，與愚有舊，且召堂審，愚竟舍去不顧。

translations.literal: The chief minister Yu Duanli was a fellow townsman, had old ties with Yu, and was about to summon him for hall examination; Yu in the end left and paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Yu Duanli, a townsman and old friend, was about to summon him for court examination; Yu simply left without responding.

sentences.zh: 結廬城南，頹坦敗壁，蓬蒿蕭然。

translations.literal: He built a hut south of the city; crumbling walls and broken partitions, mugwort and weeds desolate.
translations.idiomatic: He built a hut south of the city—crumbling walls, broken partitions, weeds everywhere.

sentences.zh: 著書自適，《書》、《禮》、《語》、《孟》皆有解。

translations.literal: He wrote books for his own ease; the Documents, Rites, Analects, and Mencius all had his commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote for his own contentment, commenting on the Documents, Rites, Analects, and Mencius.

sentences.zh: 年八十三而卒。

translations.literal: He died aged eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 故友與其門人私諡曰謙靖先生，後更諡曰靖君，鄉郡祠之。

translations.literal: Old friends and his disciples privately gave him the posthumous title Master of Modest Tranquility; later it was changed to Tranquil Lord, and the district enshrined him.
translations.idiomatic: Friends and disciples gave him the posthumous title Master of Modest Tranquility, later changed to Tranquil Lord; the district erected a shrine.

sentences.zh: 妻徐氏在家時，其母將以嫁姑子之富者，徐泣曰：“為富人妻，不願也。”

translations.literal: His wife the Lady Xu, while still at home, was to be married by her mother to her husband's sister's wealthy son; Xu wept and said, "To be a rich man's wife—I do not wish it."
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Xu, while at home, was to be married to a wealthy cousin; she wept, "I will not be a rich man's wife."

sentences.zh: 遂歸於愚，居破屋中，一事機杼。

translations.literal: She thereupon married Yu, dwelt in a broken-down house, and attended solely to the loom.
translations.idiomatic: She married Yu instead, lived in a broken-down house, and did nothing but weave.

sentences.zh: 愚嚐懷白金歸，徐怒曰：“我以子為賢而若是，亟具歸。”

translations.literal: Yu once brought white silver home in his bosom; Xu angrily said, "I took you for worthy, yet you are like this—return it at once."
translations.idiomatic: Once Yu brought silver home; Xu angrily said, "I thought you worthy—return it at once."

sentences.zh: 愚出書以示，束修得也，乃已。

translations.literal: Yu produced books to show her—it was tuition received—and only then did she stop.
translations.idiomatic: Yu showed her his books—it was tuition—and she relented.

sentences.zh: 有梁鴻之風焉。

translations.literal: She had the manner of Liang Hong.
translations.idiomatic: She had the spirit of Liang Hong and Meng Guang.

sentences.zh: 子克、幾、凡。

translations.literal: His sons were Ke, Ji, and Fan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Ke, Ji, and Fan.

sentences.zh: 克蚤以詩名，葉適嚐稱其可繼陶、韋。

translations.literal: Ke early gained fame in poetry; Ye Shi once praised him as able to succeed Tao Yuanming and Wei Yingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Ke won early fame in poetry; Ye Shi said he could follow Tao Yuanming and Wei Yingwu.

sentences.zh: 魏掞之，字子實，建州建陽人，初字元履。

translations.literal: Wei Shanzhi, style name Zishi, was a man of Jianyang in Jianzhou; his original style name was Yuanlü.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shanzhi, courtesy name Zishi, was from Jianyang in Jianzhou; his original courtesy name was Yuanlü.

sentences.zh: 自幼有大志。

translations.literal: From childhood he had great purpose.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he harbored great ambition.

sentences.zh: 師胡憲，與朱熹遊。

translations.literal: He took Hu Xian as teacher and associated with Zhu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Hu Xian and befriended Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 兩以鄉舉試禮部不第。

translations.literal: Twice on village recommendation he tested at the Ministry of Rites and did not pass.
translations.idiomatic: Twice recommended locally, he failed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 嘗客衢守章傑所。

translations.literal: He once was a guest at the home of Quzhou prefect Zhang Jie.
translations.idiomatic: He once lodged with Quzhou prefect Zhang Jie.

sentences.zh: 趙鼎以謫死，其子汾將喪過衢。

translations.literal: Zhao Ding died in banishment; his son Fen was escorting the coffin through Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding died in exile; his son Fen was escorting the coffin through Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 傑雅憾鼎，又希秦檜意，遣尉翁蒙之領卒掩取鼎平時與故舊來往簡牘。

translations.literal: Jie by nature resented Ding and also courted Qin Hui's favor; he sent the district defender Weng Mengzhi leading soldiers to seize by surprise the letters Ding had exchanged with old friends in ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: Jie resented Ding and curried favor with Qin Hui; he sent defender Weng Mengzhi with soldiers to seize Zhao Ding's correspondence with old friends.

sentences.zh: 蒙之先遣人告汾焚之，逮至一無所得。

translations.literal: Mengzhi first sent someone to tell Fen to burn them; when they arrived nothing was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Mengzhi secretly warned Fen to burn the letters; when they arrived, nothing was found.

sentences.zh: 傑怒，治蒙之，拘汾於兵家所，且以告檜。

translations.literal: Jie was angry, punished Mengzhi, detained Fen at a military lodging, and moreover reported to Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Jie punished Mengzhi, detained Fen at a military post, and reported to Qin Hui.

sentences.zh: 掞之以書責傑，長揖徑歸。

translations.literal: Shanzhi wrote a letter rebuking Jie, bowed with joined hands, and went straight home.
translations.idiomatic: Shanzhi wrote rebuking Jie, bowed, and went straight home.

sentences.zh: 築室讀書，榜以“艮齋”，自是人稱曰艮齋先生。
