translations.literal: He built a room for study and inscribed it "Gen Studio"; from this people called him Master of Gen Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He built a study hall inscribed "Gen Studio," and people called him Master of Gen Studio.

sentences.zh: 閩帥汪應辰、建守陳正同知其賢，薦於朝，時相尼之，不果召。

translations.literal: The Fujian commander Wang Yingchen and Jian prefect Chen Zhengtong knew his worth and recommended him to court, but the chief minister obstructed it and the summons did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian commander Wang Yingchen and Jian prefect Chen Zhengtong recommended him, but the chief minister blocked the summons.

sentences.zh: 乾道中，詔舉遺逸，部刺史芮燁與帥、守共表其行誼，特詔召之，掞之力辭。

translations.literal: In the Qiandao era an edict sought hidden worthies; the regional inspector Rui Ye with the commander and prefect jointly memorialized his conduct and integrity; a special edict summoned him, but Shanzhi firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: During Qiandao, an edict sought hidden worthies; inspector Rui Ye and local officials recommended him; he was specially summoned but firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 時宰相陳俊卿，閩人也，雅知掞之，招之甚力。

translations.literal: At that time the chief minister Chen Junqing was a man of Min and by nature knew Shanzhi well, recruiting him with great effort.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Chen Junqing of Fujian knew him well and pressed him hard to serve.

sentences.zh: 乃以布衣入見，極陳當時之務，大要勸上以修德業、正人心、養士氣為恢復之本。

translations.literal: He then entered audience as a commoner, fully set forth the affairs of the time, and in general urged the emperor to take cultivating virtue and achievement, rectifying people's hearts, and nurturing scholars' spirit as the foundation of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: He then appeared as a commoner and urged the emperor to make cultivating virtue, rectifying hearts, and nurturing scholarly spirit the foundation of restoration.

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之，賜同進士出身，守太學錄。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it, granted him equal jinshi status, and appointed him recorder of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted his counsel, granted him equal jinshi status, and made him Imperial Academy recorder.

sentences.zh: 先是，學官養望自高，不與諸生接。

translations.literal: Earlier, academy officials nurtured their own prestige and kept aloof, not meeting students.
translations.idiomatic: Previously academy officials held themselves aloof from students.

sentences.zh: 掞之既就職，日進諸生教誨之，又增葺其舍，人人感勵。

translations.literal: Once Shanzhi took office he daily advanced to instruct students, and also repaired and expanded their quarters; everyone was moved and encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he taught students daily and repaired their quarters; all were inspired.

sentences.zh: 將釋菜，掞之請廢王安石父子從祀，追爵程顥、程頤，列於祀典，不報。

translations.literal: When the vegetable-offering ceremony was to be held, Shanzhi requested abolishing the accompanying sacrifice to Wang Anshi and his son, posthumously ennobling Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi and listing them in the sacrificial canon—no response.
translations.idiomatic: Before the vegetable-offering ceremony he asked to remove Wang Anshi and his son from the sacrificial canon and ennoble Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi—no response.

sentences.zh: 復言“太學之教宜以德行經術為先，其次則通習世務。

translations.literal: He again said, "Imperial Academy teaching should take virtue, conduct, and classical learning as foremost; next should come mastery of worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He again urged that academy teaching should prioritize virtue and classical learning, then worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 今乃專以空言取人”，又不報。

translations.literal: Now it exclusively takes people by empty words"—again no response.
translations.idiomatic: Now it selects men by empty rhetoric alone"—again no response.

sentences.zh: 遂丐去。

translations.literal: He thereupon begged to leave.
translations.idiomatic: He then begged to resign.

sentences.zh: 會福州副總管曾覿秩滿還，在道，掞之累疏以諫，移疾杜門，遺書陳俊卿責其不能救止，語甚切。

translations.literal: It happened that Fuzhou deputy commander Zeng Di, his term ended, was returning on the road; Shanzhi repeatedly memorialized in remonstrance, pleaded illness and shut his door, and sent a letter to Chen Junqing blaming him for failing to stop it—the words very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuzhou deputy commander Zeng Di returned from his term, Shanzhi repeatedly memorialized against him, pleaded illness, shut his door, and wrote Chen Junqing a sharp letter blaming him for failing to stop it.

sentences.zh: 遂以迎親請歸，行數曰，罷為台州教授。

translations.literal: He thereupon requested return on grounds of welcoming his parents; after several days on the road he was dismissed and made professor of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to return to welcome his parents; after a few days on the road he was demoted to Taizhou professor.

sentences.zh: 方掞之之未行也，覿至國門外已久，伺掞之去，乃敢入。

translations.literal: When Shanzhi had not yet departed, Di had long been outside the capital gate, waiting until Shanzhi left before daring to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Before Shanzhi left, Di had waited outside the capital gate until Shanzhi departed before daring to enter.

sentences.zh: 掞之在朝不能半歲，既歸，喟然歎曰：“上恩深厚如此，而吾學不足以感悟聖意。”

translations.literal: Shanzhi was at court less than half a year; once returned he sighed deeply and said, "The emperor's grace is so profound, yet my learning is insufficient to move the sage mind."
translations.idiomatic: Shanzhi served less than half a year; on returning he sighed, "The emperor's grace is so deep, yet my learning cannot move his mind."

sentences.zh: 乃日居艮齋，條理舊聞，以求其所未至。

translations.literal: He then daily dwelt at Gen Studio, ordering old learning to seek what he had not yet attained.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Gen Studio daily to organize old learning and seek what he had not yet attained.

sentences.zh: 其居家，謹喪祭，重禮法。

translations.literal: In his household he was strict in mourning sacrifices and valued ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: At home he was strict in mourning rites and valued propriety.

sentences.zh: 從父有客於南者，千里迎養，死葬如禮，而字其孤。

translations.literal: His father's younger brother had a guest from the south; he welcomed and supported him from a thousand li, buried him according to rites when he died, and gave a style name to his orphan.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle's guest from the south was welcomed from afar, buried with full rites, and his orphan given a courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 建俗生子多不舉，為文以戒，全活者甚眾。

translations.literal: The custom of Jian was that many did not rear newborn sons; he wrote a text to warn against this, and very many were preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: Jian custom favored infant abandonment; his warning essay saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 又白於官，請督不葬其親者，富與期，貧與財，而無主後者掩之。

translations.literal: He also informed the officials, requesting supervision of those who did not bury their kin—giving the wealthy deadlines, the poor funds, and burying those with no heirs to maintain sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He urged officials to compel burial of the unburied—deadlines for the rich, funds for the poor, and burial for those without heirs.

sentences.zh: 每遇歲饑，為粥以食饑者。

translations.literal: Whenever famine years came he made gruel to feed the hungry.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years he served gruel to the hungry.

sentences.zh: 後依古社倉法，請官米以貸民，至冬取之以納於倉。

translations.literal: Later, following the ancient communal granary method, he requested official grain to lend the people; in winter they took it to repay into the granary.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed the ancient communal granary method, borrowing official grain to lend the people for winter repayment.

sentences.zh: 部使者素敬掞之，捐米千餘斛假之，歲歲斂散如常，民賴以濟。

translations.literal: The circuit envoy had always respected Shanzhi and donated more than a thousand bushels of rice to lend him; year by year collection and distribution went as usual, and the people relied on it for relief.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit envoy, who respected him, lent more than a thousand bushels yearly; the people relied on it for relief.

sentences.zh: 諸鄉社倉自掞之始。

translations.literal: Communal granaries in the various districts began with Shanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Communal granaries in the region began with Shanzhi.

sentences.zh: 與人交，嘉其善而救其失。

translations.literal: In associating with people he praised their good and rescued their faults.
translations.idiomatic: In friendship he praised others' virtues and corrected their faults.

sentences.zh: 後進以禮來者，苟有寸長，必汲汲推挽成就之。

translations.literal: Juniors who came with courtesy—if they had the slightest merit, he would urgently push and draw them to achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Juniors who approached with courtesy—if they showed the slightest talent—he urgently helped them succeed.

sentences.zh: 至或訾其近名，則蹙然曰：“使夫人而避此嫌，為善之路絕矣。”

translations.literal: When some blamed him for courting fame he would frown and say, "If people avoid this suspicion, the path of doing good is cut off."
translations.idiomatic: When accused of courting fame he frowned and said, "If one avoids that suspicion, the path of goodness is closed."

sentences.zh: 病革，母視之，不巾不見。

translations.literal: When critically ill, if his mother came to see him he would not receive her without his headcloth.
translations.idiomatic: When gravely ill he would not receive his mother without his cap.

sentences.zh: 戒其子“毋以僧巫俗禮浼我。”

translations.literal: He admonished his sons, "Do not defile me with Buddhist monks, shamans, or vulgar rites."
translations.idiomatic: He warned his sons, "Do not defile me with Buddhist or shamanistic vulgar rites."

sentences.zh: 以書召朱熹至，委以後事而訣。

translations.literal: He summoned Zhu Xi by letter, entrusted him with later affairs, and took leave.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Zhu Xi by letter, entrusted his affairs to him, and bade farewell.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: He died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 後上思其直諒，將召用之，大臣言已死，乃贈直秘閣。

translations.literal: Later the emperor thought of his frank sincerity and was about to summon and employ him; a great minister said he was already dead, and he was posthumously granted Directorship of the Secretariat Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor, remembering his frankness, meant to recall him; told he was dead, he was posthumously granted Directorship of the Secretariat Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 熹平日趣向與掞之同。

translations.literal: Xi's daily orientation and Shanzhi's were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's inclinations matched Shanzhi's.

sentences.zh: 乾道中，熹亦被召，將行，聞掞之去國，乃止。

translations.literal: In the Qiandao era Xi was also summoned; about to depart, he heard Shanzhi had left the state and thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: During Qiandao, Xi was also summoned; hearing Shanzhi had left court, he stayed home.

sentences.zh: 青城山道人安世通者，本西人。

translations.literal: The Daoist of Mount Qingcheng, An Shitong, was originally a man of the western regions.
translations.idiomatic: An Shitong, a Daoist of Mount Qingcheng, was originally from the western regions.

sentences.zh: 其父有謀策，為武官，數以言幹當路不用，遂自沈於酒而終。

translations.literal: His father had stratagems and plans, was a military officer, and several times offered counsel to those in power but was not used; he thereupon drowned himself in wine and died.
translations.idiomatic: His father, a military officer with strategic talent, repeatedly offered counsel to those in power but was ignored, and drank himself to death.

sentences.zh: 世通亦隱居青城山中不出。

translations.literal: Shitong also lived in seclusion on Mount Qingcheng and did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Shitong too lived in seclusion on Mount Qingcheng and never emerged.

sentences.zh: 吳曦反，乃獻書於成都帥楊輔曰：“世通在山中，忽聞關外之變，不覺大慟。

translations.literal: When Wu Xi rebelled he presented a letter to the Chengdu commander Yang Fu, saying, "Shitong is in the mountains; suddenly hearing of the change beyond the passes, I could not help great lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xi rebelled he wrote Chengdu commander Yang Fu: "In the mountains I heard of the crisis beyond the passes and could not restrain my grief.

sentences.zh: 世通雖方外人，而大人先生亦嚐發以入道之門。

translations.literal: Though Shitong is an outsider to the realm, great men have also once opened for him the gate of entering the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am an outsider, great men have opened the gate of the Way to me.

sentences.zh: 竊以為公初得曦檄，即當還書，誦其家世，激以忠義，聚官屬軍民，素服號慟，因而散金發粟，鼓集忠義，閉劍門，檄夔、梓，興仗義之師，以順討逆，誰不願從？

translations.literal: I venture to think that when you first received Xi's dispatch you should at once have returned a letter, recited his family background, roused him with loyalty and righteousness, gathered officials, troops, and civilians, worn plain dress and cried out in grief, and thereby distributed gold and issued grain, roused loyal righteousness, closed Jianmen Pass, sent proclamations to Kui and Zi, and raised an army of righteous duty to punish the rebel with legitimacy—who would not wish to follow?
translations.idiomatic: When you first received Xi's dispatch you should have replied, recited his lineage, roused loyalty, gathered officials and troops in mourning dress, distributed gold and grain, closed Jianmen Pass, summoned Kui and Zi, and raised a righteous army—who would not follow?

sentences.zh: 而士大夫皆酒缸飯囊，不明大義，尚雲少屈以保生靈，何其不知輕重如此！

translations.literal: Yet the scholar-officials are all wine vats and rice bags, unclear on the great principle, still saying one should bend slightly to preserve the people—how can they be so ignorant of what weighs heavy and light!
translations.idiomatic: Yet scholar-officials are wine vats and rice bags, blind to principle, still saying bend a little to save the people—how can they be so blind to what matters!

sentences.zh: 夫君乃父也，民乃子也，豈有棄父而救子之理？

translations.literal: The ruler is the father; the people are the sons—how can there be principle in abandoning the father to save the sons?
translations.idiomatic: The ruler is father, the people sons—how can one abandon the father to save the sons?

sentences.zh: 此非曦一人之叛，乃舉蜀士大夫之叛也。

translations.literal: This is not the rebellion of Xi alone; it is the rebellion of all Shu scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: This is not Xi's rebellion alone but the rebellion of all Shu scholar-officials.

sentences.zh: 聞古有叛民無叛官，今曦叛而士大夫皆縮手以聽命，是驅民而為叛也。

translations.literal: I have heard that in antiquity there were rebellious people but no rebellious officials; now Xi rebels yet scholar-officials all shrink back and obey orders—this is driving the people to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity knew rebellious people but not rebellious officials; now officials shrink back and obey Xi—driving the people to rebel.

sentences.zh: 且曦雖叛逆，猶有所忌，未敢建正朔、殺士大夫，尚以虛文見招，亦以公之與否卜民之從違也。

translations.literal: Moreover, though Xi is rebellious he still has scruples, has not dared to establish a calendar or kill scholar-officials, and still uses empty formalities to invite them—also taking whether you assent or not as a divination of whether the people will follow or resist.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xi rebels he still fears to establish a calendar or kill officials, and still invites you with empty formalities—testing whether the people will follow by whether you assent.

sentences.zh: 今悠悠不決，徒為婦人女子之悲，所謂停囚長智，吾恐朝廷之失望也。

translations.literal: Now you drift without decision, merely giving way to the grief of women and girls—what is called delaying the prisoner to grow clever; I fear the court will be disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Now you hesitate endlessly, indulging womanish grief—delaying only strengthens the rebel; I fear the court will be disappointed.

sentences.zh: 凡舉大事者，成敗死生皆當付之度外。

translations.literal: Whoever undertakes great affairs must set success and failure, life and death, outside consideration.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever undertakes great affairs must set success, failure, life, and death beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 區區行年五十二矣，古人言：‘可以生而生，福也；

translations.literal: I am but fifty-two years old; the ancients said: 'To live when one may live is fortune;
translations.idiomatic: I am only fifty-two; the ancients said: 'To live when one may live is fortune;

sentences.zh: 可以死而死，亦福也。

translations.literal: to die when one may die is also fortune.
translations.idiomatic: to die when one may die is also fortune.

sentences.zh: ’決不忍汗麵戴天，同為叛民也。”

translations.literal: I absolutely cannot bear to sweat my face while wearing Heaven on my head and become a rebel together with them.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear to live under Heaven's canopy as a rebel alongside them.

sentences.zh: 輔有重名，蜀中士大夫多勸以舉義者，而世通之言尤切至。

translations.literal: Fu had a weighty reputation; many scholar-officials in Shu urged him to raise righteous arms, and Shitong's words were especially penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: Fu enjoyed great renown; many Shu officials urged righteous action, and Shitong's words were especially forceful.

sentences.zh: 輔不能決，遂東如江陵，請吳獵舉兵以討曦。

translations.literal: Fu could not decide, and thereupon went east to Jiangling, requesting Wu Lie to raise troops to punish Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to decide, Fu went east to Jiangling and asked Wu Lie to raise troops against Xi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，曦敗，獵使蜀，薦士以世通為首雲。

translations.literal: Before long Xi was defeated; Lie sent envoys to Shu and recommended scholars with Shitong at their head.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xi was defeated; Lie sent envoys to Shu and recommended scholars, naming Shitong first.

sentences.zh: ◎卓行○劉庭式巢穀徐積曾叔卿劉永一

translations.literal: ◎ Outstanding Conduct ○ Liu Tingshi, Chao Gu, Xu Ji, Zeng Shuqing, Liu Yongyi
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Outstanding Conduct ○ Liu Tingshi, Chao Gu, Xu Ji, Zeng Shuqing, and Liu Yongyi

sentences.zh: 父子有親，夫婦有別，朋友有信，天下之所共知而共由者也，乃有卓行於斯焉。

translations.literal: Father and son have affection, husband and wife have distinction, friend and friend have trust—these all-under-Heaven commonly knows and commonly follows—yet there are outstanding acts in these very relations.
translations.idiomatic: Affection between father and son, distinction between husband and wife, trust between friends—these all the world knows—yet outstanding conduct appears even here.

sentences.zh: 徐積於其所天，劉庭式於其室家，巢穀於其知己，皆行常人之難。

translations.literal: Xu Ji toward his Heaven-appointed parent, Liu Tingshi toward his household, Chao Gu toward his intimate friend—all performed what ordinary men find hard.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ji toward his parent, Liu Tingshi toward his household, Chao Gu toward his friend—all did what ordinary men find hard.

sentences.zh: 行其所難而安焉，豈非卓乎？

translations.literal: To perform what is hard and be at ease in it—is this not outstanding?
translations.idiomatic: To do the hard thing and be at peace—is that not outstanding?

sentences.zh: 曾叔卿之不欺，劉永一之不苟取，皆以一事而人譽之終身，蓋有其所矣，其可忽諸！

translations.literal: Zeng Shuqing's refusal to deceive and Liu Yongyi's refusal to take unrightfully—both by a single act won lifelong praise from others; surely they had their grounds—how can these be neglected!
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Shuqing's honesty and Liu Yongyi's integrity won lifelong praise from single acts—surely they had their reasons; how can we neglect them!

sentences.zh: 撰《卓行傳》。

translations.literal: I compose the Biographies of Outstanding Conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Thus I compose the Biographies of Outstanding Conduct.

sentences.zh: 劉庭式，字得之，齊州人，舉進士。

translations.literal: Liu Tingshi, style name Dezhi, was a man of Qizhou and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tingshi, courtesy name Dezhi, was from Qizhou and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾守密州，庭式為通判。

translations.literal: When Su Shi was prefect of Mizhou, Tingshi was administrative vice-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi governed Mizhou, Tingshi served as vice-prefect.

sentences.zh: 初，庭式未第時，議娶鄉人之女，既約，未納幣。

translations.literal: Earlier, before Tingshi passed the examination, he agreed to marry a village man's daughter; the engagement was made but bride-price not yet paid.
translations.idiomatic: Before passing the examination he betrothed a village girl; the engagement was made but bride-price not yet paid.

sentences.zh: 庭式乃及第，女以病喪明，女家躬耕貧甚，不敢復言。

translations.literal: Tingshi then passed; the girl through illness lost her sight; the girl's family plowed by hand and were extremely poor and did not dare speak again.
translations.idiomatic: Tingshi then passed the examination; the girl went blind from illness; her impoverished family farmed by hand and dared not raise the matter again.

sentences.zh: 或勸納其幼女，庭式笑曰：“吾心已許之矣，豈可負吾初心哉。”

translations.literal: Some urged him to take her younger sister; Tingshi laughed and said, "My heart has already pledged to her—how could I betray my original intent?"
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to marry her younger sister; Tingshi laughed, "My heart is pledged to her—how could I betray my first promise?"

sentences.zh: 卒娶之。

translations.literal: In the end he married her.
translations.idiomatic: He married her in the end.

sentences.zh: 生數子，後死，庭式喪之逾年，不肯復娶。

translations.literal: She bore several sons and later died; Tingshi mourned her more than a year and would not remarry.
translations.idiomatic: She bore several sons and died; Tingshi mourned more than a year and would not remarry.

sentences.zh: 軾問之曰：“哀生於愛，愛生於色。

translations.literal: Shi asked him, "Grief arises from love, love arises from beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi asked, "Grief arises from love, love from beauty.

sentences.zh: 今君愛何從生，哀何從出乎？”

translations.literal: Now from what does your lordship's love arise, and from what does grief emerge?
translations.idiomatic: From what does your love arise, and from what your grief?

sentences.zh: 庭式曰：“吾知喪吾妻而已。

translations.literal: Tingshi said, "I know only that I have lost my wife.
translations.idiomatic: Tingshi said, "I know only that I have lost my wife.

sentences.zh: 吾若緣色而生愛，緣愛而生哀，色衰愛弛，吾哀亦忘，則凡揚袂倚市，目挑而心招者，皆可以為妻也耶？”

translations.literal: If I loved because of beauty and grieved because of love, when beauty faded love would slacken and my grief would also be forgotten—then could every woman who lifts her sleeve at the market and beckons with eye and heart all become my wife?
translations.idiomatic: If I loved for beauty and grieved for love, when beauty faded love would fade and grief with it—then could every market flirt become my wife?

sentences.zh: 軾深感其言。

translations.literal: Shi was deeply moved by his words.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 庭式後監太平觀，老於廬山，絕粒不食，目奕奕有紫光，步上下峻阪如飛，以高壽終。

translations.literal: Tingshi later supervised the Taiping Abbey, aged on Mount Lu, abstained from grain and did not eat; his eyes sparkled with purple light, and walking up and down steep slopes he was like flying; he ended in great longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Later he supervised Taiping Abbey, aged on Mount Lu, abstained from grain; his eyes shone with purple light, he scaled steep slopes like flight, and died at a great age.

sentences.zh: 巢穀，初名穀，字元修，眉州眉山人。

translations.literal: Chao Gu, original name Gu, style name Yuanxiu, was a man of Meishan in Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Gu, original name Gu, courtesy name Yuanxiu, was from Meishan in Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 父中，穀傳其學，雖樸而博。

translations.literal: His father Zhong; Gu transmitted his learning—though plain, it was broad.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhong; Gu inherited his learning—plain but broad.

sentences.zh: 舉進士京師。

translations.literal: He presented himself for the jinshi examination in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi examination in the capital.

sentences.zh: 穀素多力，見舉武藝者心好之，遂棄其舊學，蓄弓箭，習騎射，久之業成而不中第。

translations.literal: Gu from of old had great strength; seeing those who presented military arts he took it to heart, abandoned his former learning, stored bow and arrows, practiced mounted archery; after long effort he mastered the art but did not pass.
translations.idiomatic: Naturally strong, he admired military candidates, abandoned literary study, took up archery and horsemanship, mastered the arts but failed the examination.

sentences.zh: 聞西邊多驍勇，為四方冠，去遊秦鳳、涇原間。

translations.literal: He heard the western frontier had many fierce warriors, foremost in the four directions, and went to roam between Qinfeng and Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the western frontier bred the empire's fiercest warriors, he traveled between Qinfeng and Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 所至友其秀桀，與韓存寶尤相善，教之兵書。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he befriended the outstanding and heroic; with Han Cunbao he was especially close and taught him military books.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went he befriended the bold; he was especially close to Han Cunbao and taught him military texts.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，存寶為河州將，有功，號熙河名將。

translations.literal: In the Xining era Cunbao was a general of Hezhou, had merit, and was called a famous general of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: During Xining, Cunbao became a Hezhou general with merit and was famed on the Xihe frontier.

sentences.zh: 會滬州蠻乞弟擾邊，諸郡不能製，命存寶出兵討之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Huzhou barbarian Qidi disturbed the border; the various prefectures could not control him, and Cunbao was ordered to lead troops to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huzhou chieftain Qidi raided the border and prefectures could not suppress him, Cunbao was ordered to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 存寶不習蠻事，邀穀至軍中問焉。

translations.literal: Cunbao was not versed in barbarian affairs and invited Gu to the army to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Unversed in tribal warfare, Cunbao invited Gu to camp for counsel.

sentences.zh: 及存寶得罪，將就逮，自度必死，謂穀曰：“我涇原武夫，死非所惜。

translations.literal: When Cunbao was found guilty and about to be arrested, judging himself certain to die he said to Gu, "I am a Jingyuan fighting man; death is not what I regret.
translations.idiomatic: When Cunbao was condemned and about to be arrested, expecting death he told Gu, "I am a Jingyuan soldier; death does not trouble me.

sentences.zh: 顧妻子不免寒餓，橐中有銀數百兩，非君莫可使遺之者。”

translations.literal: I only fear my wife and children will not escape cold and hunger; in my bag are several hundred taels of silver—no one but you can be entrusted to deliver them.
translations.idiomatic: I fear only that my wife and children will starve; I have several hundred taels of silver—no one but you can deliver them.

sentences.zh: 穀許諾，即變姓名，懷銀步往授其子，人無知者。

translations.literal: Gu promised, changed his name at once, carried the silver on foot to give to his son, and no one knew.
translations.idiomatic: Gu agreed, changed his name, walked the silver to Cunbao's son, and no one knew.

sentences.zh: 存寶死，穀逃避江、淮間，會赦乃出。

translations.literal: When Cunbao died, Gu fled and hid between the Yangzi and Huai; when an amnesty came he emerged.
translations.idiomatic: After Cunbao's death Gu hid between the Yangzi and Huai until an amnesty let him emerge.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾謫黃州，與穀同鄉，幼而識之，因與之遊。

translations.literal: When Su Shi was banished to Huangzhou he was Gu's fellow townsman and had known him from youth, and therefore associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi was exiled to Huangzhou, he and Gu were fellow townsmen who had known each other since youth and became companions.

sentences.zh: 乃軾與弟轍在朝，穀浮沉裏中，未嚐一來相見。

translations.literal: Yet when Shi and his younger brother Zhe were at court, Gu drifted in the village and never once came to see them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the Su brothers held office, Gu stayed in the village and never once came to call.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，軾、轍謫嶺海，平生親舊無復相聞者，穀獨慨然自眉山誦言欲徒步訪兩蘇，聞者皆笑其狂。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng, Shi and Zhe were banished to the Lingnan coast; lifelong kin and friends no longer exchanged word—but Gu alone, moved, declared from Meishan that he wished to visit the two Su on foot; those who heard all laughed at his madness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shaosheng, when the Su brothers were exiled to the far south and old friends fell silent, Gu alone declared from Meishan that he would visit them on foot; all who heard laughed at his madness.

sentences.zh: 元符二年，穀竟往，至梅州遺轍書曰：“我萬里步行見公，不意自全，今至梅矣，不旬日必見，死無恨矣。”

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfu Gu actually went; reaching Meizhou he sent Zhe a letter saying, "I have walked ten thousand li to see you, not expecting to survive intact; now I have reached Mei; within ten days I shall surely see you—I can die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfu year 2 Gu set out; reaching Meizhou he wrote Zhe: "I have walked ten thousand li to see you; now I am at Mei and shall see you within ten days—then I can die without regret."

sentences.zh: 轍驚喜曰：“此非今世人，古之人也。”

translations.literal: Zhe said in surprise and joy, "This is not a man of today's world—he is a man of antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Zhe exclaimed in joy, "This is not a man of our age but of antiquity."

sentences.zh: 既見，握手相泣，已而道平生，逾月不厭。

translations.literal: When they met they clasped hands and wept; then they spoke of their whole lives for more than a month without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: When they met they wept hand in hand and talked of their lives for more than a month without tiring.

sentences.zh: 時穀年七十三，瘦瘠多病，將復見軾於海南，轍湣而止之曰：“君意則善，然循至儋數千里，當復渡海，非老人事也。”

translations.literal: At that time Gu was seventy-three, thin and sickly, and was about to see Shi again in Hainan; Zhe pitied him and stopped him, saying, "Your intent is good, but following on to Dan is several thousand li more and you must cross the sea again—this is not an old man's affair."
translations.idiomatic: Gu was seventy-three, frail and ill, and meant to see Shi in Hainan; Zhe pitied him and said, "Your heart is good, but Dan is thousands of li farther and you must cross the sea again—not work for an old man."

sentences.zh: 穀曰：“我自視未即死也，公無止我。”

translations.literal: Gu said, "I do not see myself about to die—do not stop me."
translations.idiomatic: Gu said, "I do not see myself dying yet—do not stop me."

sentences.zh: 閱其橐中無數千錢，轍方困乏，亦強資遣之。

translations.literal: Seeing his bag held not several thousand cash, and Zhe himself was in hardship, he still forced himself to supply travel funds.
translations.idiomatic: Finding his bag nearly empty and himself in hardship, Zhe still forced money on him for the journey.

sentences.zh: 舟行至新會，有蠻隸竊其橐裝以逃，獲於新州，穀從之至新，遂病死。

translations.literal: Traveling by boat to Xinhui, a barbarian servant stole his baggage and fled; captured at Xinzhou, Gu followed on to Xin and thereupon died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Sailing to Xinhui, a servant stole his baggage; captured at Xinzhou, Gu followed to Xin and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 轍聞，哭之失聲，恨不用己言而致死，又奇其不用己言而行其誌也。

translations.literal: When Zhe heard he wept aloud, regretting that his words were not heeded and led to death, yet also marveling that without heeding his words Gu carried out his purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Zhe wept aloud, grieving that his counsel was ignored yet marveling that Gu fulfilled his purpose despite it.

sentences.zh: 徐積，字仲車，楚州山陽人。

translations.literal: Xu Ji, style name Zhongche, was a man of Shanyang in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ji, courtesy name Zhongche, was from Shanyang in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝行出於天稟。

translations.literal: His filial conduct issued from Heaven's endowment.
translations.idiomatic: His filial devotion was inborn.

sentences.zh: 三歲父死，旦旦求之甚哀，母使讀《孝經》，輒淚落不能止。

translations.literal: At three his father died; each morning he sought him with great grief; his mother had him read the Classic of Filial Piety and he would shed tears that would not stop.
translations.idiomatic: His father died when he was three; each morning he grieved deeply; when his mother had him read the Classic of Filial Piety he wept without stopping.

sentences.zh: 事母至孝，朝夕冠帶定省。

translations.literal: In serving his mother he was supremely filial, morning and evening in cap and sash paying respects.
translations.idiomatic: He served his mother with supreme filial piety, attending her morning and evening in full dress.

sentences.zh: 從胡翼之學。

translations.literal: He followed Hu Yizhi in study.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Hu Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 所居一室，寒一衲裘，啜菽飲水，翼之饋以食，弗受。

translations.literal: He dwelt in one room, cold in a single patched robe, sipping beans and drinking water; Yizhi sent him food and he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in one room, cold in a patched robe, eating beans and drinking water; he refused food sent by Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 應舉入都，不忍舍其親，徒載而西。

translations.literal: Answering the examination he entered the capital but could not bear to leave his parent and went west on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Taking the examination he went to the capital on foot, unable to leave his mother.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，舉首許安國率同年生入拜，且致百金為壽，謝卻之。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination; the top graduate Xu Anguo led the men of the same year to pay respects and also sent a hundred in gold as congratulations; he declined.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi; top graduate Xu Anguo led classmates to congratulate him with a hundred in gold, which he refused.

sentences.zh: 以父名“石”終身不用石器，行遇石則避而不踐，或問之，積曰：“吾遇之則怵然傷吾心，思吾親，故不忍加足其上爾。”

translations.literal: Because his father's name was "Stone" he never used stone implements all his life; walking, when he met stone he avoided and did not tread on it; when asked, Ji said, "When I meet it I am suddenly wounded in heart, thinking of my parent—therefore I cannot bear to set foot upon it."
translations.idiomatic: Because his father's name was Stone he never used stone implements; encountering stone on the road he avoided it, saying, "It wounds my heart and reminds me of my father—I cannot tread on it."

sentences.zh: 母亡，水漿不入口者七日，悲慟嘔血。

translations.literal: When his mother died he took neither water nor gruel for seven days, grieving until he vomited blood.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he took no food or water for seven days and vomited blood from grief.

sentences.zh: 廬墓三年，臥苫枕塊，衰絰不去體，雪夜伏墓側，哭不絕音。

translations.literal: He kept vigil at the tomb three years, lying on rush mat with head on clod, mourning garments never leaving his body; on snowy nights he lay beside the tomb, weeping without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He kept tomb vigil three years on a rush mat with a clod for a pillow, never removing mourning dress; on snowy nights he lay by the tomb weeping without cease.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士呂溱過其廬適聞之，為泣下曰：“使鬼神有知，亦垂涕也。”

translations.literal: Hanlin academician Lü Zhen passed his hut and happened to hear it; he wept and said, "If spirits have knowledge they too would shed tears."
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Lü Zhen passed his hut, heard him weeping, and said, "If spirits have knowledge they too would weep."

sentences.zh: 甘露歲降兆域，杏兩枝合為幹。

translations.literal: Sweet dew descended yearly on the tomb precinct; two apricot branches joined into one trunk.
translations.idiomatic: Sweet dew fell yearly on the tomb; two apricot branches merged into one trunk.

sentences.zh: 既終喪，不徹筵幾，起居饋獻如平生。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he did not remove the mat and table; in rising, resting, and offering food it was as in life.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended he kept the mat and table set, attending his mother in daily routine as if she were alive.

sentences.zh: 中年有聵疾，屏處窮裏，而四方事無不知。

translations.literal: In mid-life he had deafness, lived secluded in a poor lane, yet knew nothing of affairs in the four directions that he did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Deaf in middle age, he lived secluded in a poor lane yet knew affairs throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 客從南越來，積與論嶺表山川險易、鎮戍疏密，口誦手畫，若數一二。

translations.literal: A guest came from southern Yue; Ji discussed with him the mountains and rivers of Lingnan, their dangers and ease, the density and sparsity of garrisons—reciting and drawing with his hand as if counting one by one.
translations.idiomatic: A guest from the far south discussed Lingnan geography and garrison dispositions with him; Ji recited and sketched them as if counting on his fingers.

sentences.zh: 客歎曰：“不出戶而知天下，徐公是也。”

translations.literal: The guest sighed and said, "To know all-under-Heaven without leaving the door—Master Xu is such a one."
translations.idiomatic: The guest sighed, "To know the world without leaving one's door—that is Master Xu."

sentences.zh: 自少及老，日作一詩，為文率用腹稿，口占授其子。

translations.literal: From youth to old age he composed one poem daily; in writing he generally used compositions held in the belly, dictating orally to his son.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to old age he wrote a poem daily, composing in his mind and dictating to his son.

sentences.zh: 嚐借人書策，經宿還之，借者紿言中有金葉，積謝而不辨，賣衣償之。

translations.literal: He once borrowed someone's books and returned them after a night; the borrower falsely said there were gold leaves within; Ji thanked him and did not dispute it, selling clothes to compensate.
translations.idiomatic: Once he returned borrowed books overnight; the lender falsely claimed gold leaves were missing; Ji did not dispute it and sold clothes to compensate.

sentences.zh: 鄉人有爭訟，多就取決。

translations.literal: When villagers had lawsuits many came to him for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers brought disputes to him for judgment.

sentences.zh: 州以行聞，詔賜粟帛。

translations.literal: The prefecture reported his conduct and an edict bestowed grain and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture reported his conduct and the court bestowed grain and silk.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，近臣合言：“積養親以孝著，居鄉以廉稱，道義文學，顯於東南。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou, close ministers jointly said, "Ji is famed for nurturing parents with filial piety, renowned in the village for integrity; his moral principle and literary learning shine in the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou, courtiers said, "Ji is famed for filial piety, renowned for integrity, and distinguished in learning throughout the southeast.

sentences.zh: 今年過五十，以耳疾不能出仕。

translations.literal: This year he is past fifty and because of ear illness cannot take office.
translations.idiomatic: Past fifty, he cannot serve because of deafness.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方詔舉中外學官，如積之賢，宜在所表。”

translations.literal: The court is now ordering recommendation of academic officials within and without; a worthy like Ji should be among those recommended.
translations.idiomatic: The court is seeking academic officials; a worthy like Ji should be recommended.

sentences.zh: 乃以揚州司戶參軍為楚州教授。

translations.literal: He was thereupon made professor of Chuzhou from his post as revenue adjutant of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Chuzhou professor from his post as Yangzhou revenue adjutant.

sentences.zh: 每升堂，訓諸生曰：“諸君欲為君子，而勞己之力，費己之財，如此而不為，猶之可也；

translations.literal: Each time he ascended the hall he instructed the students, "You gentlemen wish to be gentlemen yet toil your strength and spend your wealth—if with such effort you still do not act, that may be forgiven;
translations.idiomatic: Each lecture he told students, "If you wish to be gentlemen and must labor and spend to do so, failure is understandable;

sentences.zh: 不勞己之力，不費己之財，何不為君子？

translations.literal: if you do not toil your strength or spend your wealth, why not be gentlemen?
translations.idiomatic: but without labor or expense, why not be gentlemen?

sentences.zh: 鄉人賤之，父母惡之，如此而不為，可也。

translations.literal: If villagers despise you and parents detest you, not acting in such case is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: If neighbors despise you and parents disapprove, not acting is acceptable.

sentences.zh: 鄉人榮之，父母欲之，何不為君子？”

translations.literal: If villagers honor you and parents desire it, why not be gentlemen?
translations.idiomatic: But if neighbors honor you and parents desire it, why not be gentlemen?

sentences.zh: 又曰：“言其所善，行其所善，思其所善，如此而不為君子者，未之有也。

translations.literal: He also said, "Speak what is good, act what is good, think what is good—one who does this and is not a gentleman has never existed.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Speak, act, and think what is good—no one who does this fails to become a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 言其不善，行其不善，思其不善，如此而不為小人者，未之有也。”

translations.literal: Speak what is not good, act what is not good, think what is not good—one who does this and is not a petty man has never existed.
translations.idiomatic: Speak, act, and think what is evil—no one who does this fails to become a petty man.

sentences.zh: 聞之者斂衽敬聽。

translations.literal: Those who heard straightened their robes and listened respectfully.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners straightened their robes and listened in respect.

sentences.zh: 居數歲，使者又交薦之，轉和州防禦推官，改宣德郎，監中嶽廟。

translations.literal: After several years envoys again recommended him in turn; he was transferred to defense push-official of Hezhou, changed to Court Gentleman for Promulgating Virtue, and supervised the Central Marchmount shrine.
translations.idiomatic: After several years envoys recommended him again; he became Hezhou defense push-official, then Promulgating Virtue Gentleman and supervisor of the Central Marchmount shrine.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 政和六年，賜諡節孝處士，官其一子。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenghe he was granted the posthumous title Reclusive Gentleman of Integrity and Filial Piety, and one son was given office.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe year 6 he was posthumously titled Reclusive Gentleman of Integrity and Filial Piety, and one son received office.

sentences.zh: 曾叔卿，建昌南豐人，鞏族兄也。

translations.literal: Zeng Shuqing was a man of Nanfeng in Jianchang, an elder clansman of the Zeng family of Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Shuqing was from Nanfeng in Jianchang, an elder kinsman of the Zeng clan.

sentences.zh: 家苦貧，即心存不欺。

translations.literal: His family was bitterly poor, yet his heart held refusal to deceive.
translations.idiomatic: Though his family was desperately poor, his heart refused deceit.

sentences.zh: 嚐買西江陶器，欲貿易於北方，既而不果行。

translations.literal: He once bought Xijiang pottery, intending to trade it in the north, but in the end did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He once bought Xijiang pottery to trade north but in the end did not go.

sentences.zh: 有從之轉售者，與之。

translations.literal: Someone who followed him wished to resell it; he gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Someone wished to resell it for him; he let him have it.

sentences.zh: 既受直矣，問將何之，其人曰：“欲效君前策耳。”

translations.literal: After payment was received he asked where he would go; the man said, "I wish to follow your former plan."
translations.idiomatic: After payment he asked the man's plans; the man said, "I mean to follow your former plan."

sentences.zh: 叔卿曰：“不可。

translations.literal: Shuqing said, "It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Shuqing said, "You cannot.

sentences.zh: 吾聞北方新有災饉，此物必不時泄，故不以行。

translations.literal: I have heard the north has newly suffered famine; this ware surely cannot be sold in season—therefore I did not go.
translations.idiomatic: I hear the north has newly suffered famine; this ware cannot be sold in time—that is why I did not go.

sentences.zh: 餘豈宜不告以誤子。”

translations.literal: How could I fail to tell you and mislead you?
translations.idiomatic: How could I fail to tell you and mislead you?

sentences.zh: 其人即取錢去。

translations.literal: The man at once took back the money and left.
translations.idiomatic: The man took back his money and left.

sentences.zh: 居鄉介潔，非所宜受，一介不取。

translations.literal: Living in the village he was upright and clean; what was not fitting to receive he would not take—a single thing he did not take.
translations.idiomatic: Upright in the village, he would not take what was not rightfully his—not the slightest thing.

sentences.zh: 妻子困於饑寒，而拊庇孤煢，唯恐失其意。

translations.literal: His wife and children suffered hunger and cold, yet he comforted and sheltered the orphaned and alone, fearing only to fail their intent.
translations.idiomatic: Though his wife and children suffered hunger and cold, he sheltered orphans and feared only to fail them.

sentences.zh: 起家進士，至著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He rose from jinshi to assistant editor in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from jinshi to Palace Library assistant editor.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，卒。

translations.literal: In the Xining era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during Xining.

sentences.zh: 劉永一，陝州夏縣人。

translations.literal: Liu Yongyi was a man of Xia county in Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yongyi was from Xia county in Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝友廉謹。

translations.literal: He was filial and brotherly, incorrupt and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: He was filial, brotherly, incorrupt, and cautious.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，巫鹹水溢入縣城，民多溺死。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining the Wuxian River overflowed into the county seat and many people drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xining the Wuxian River flooded the county seat and many people drowned.

sentences.zh: 永一持竿立門前，見他人物流入者輒擿出之。

translations.literal: Yongyi stood at his door holding a pole; whenever he saw others or goods swept in he would hook them out.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyi stood at his door with a pole and pulled out anyone or anything swept past.

sentences.zh: 有僧寓錢數萬於其室，無何而僧死，永一詣縣自言，請以錢歸其弟子。

translations.literal: A monk had lodged several tens of thousands in cash in his house; before long the monk died; Yongyi went to the county himself to report it and asked that the money be returned to his disciples.
translations.idiomatic: A monk had left tens of thousands in cash in his house; when the monk died Yongyi went to the magistrate and asked that the money be returned to his disciples.

sentences.zh: 鄉人負債不肯償，立焚其券。

translations.literal: A villager owed a debt and would not repay; he immediately burned the bond.
translations.idiomatic: When a neighbor refused to repay a debt, he burned the IOU on the spot.

sentences.zh: 行事類此。

translations.literal: His conduct was of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct was always of this kind.

sentences.zh: 兄大為，醫助教。

translations.literal: His elder brother Dawei was assistant instructor in medicine.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Dawei was an assistant instructor in medicine.

sentences.zh: 居親喪，不飲酒食肉，終三年。

translations.literal: In keeping mourning for a parent he did not drink wine or eat meat for the full three years.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning for a parent he abstained from wine and meat for the full three years.

sentences.zh: 司馬光傳之，以為今士大夫所難。

translations.literal: Sima Guang transmitted this, considering it what scholar-officials of today find difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang recorded this, holding it up as what today's scholar-officials find hard to match.
